tools.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm – Management
tools.evidence: It really does help. Now in this episode I'm [Name] a topic that's been requested by one of our listeners and many thanks for this great suggestion. So an aneurysm is essentially a permanent irreversible dilatation of a blood vessel by at least 50% of its normal expected.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Screening: NHS AAA screening men 65+. Palpation unreliable for detection.
2. If suspected: USS aorta. Risk factors: smoking, hypertension, family history. NICE NG156, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Small (3–5.4 cm): Annual surveillance USS. Optimise CV risk (statin, BP, smoking cessation).
2. Large (≥5.5 cm or symptomatic): Urgent vascular referral. NICE NG156.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Ruptured or symptomatic (pain, hypotension). 2WW: ≥5.5 cm or rapid expansion. NICE NG156.

tools.title: AF – anticoagulation choice
tools.evidence: NICE NG196: CHA2DS2-VASc for stroke prevention; DOAC first-line. Rate control (beta-blocker/CCB); rhythm control or ablation via cardiology.

options.label: Assess Risk (CHA2DS2-VASc)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Grade):
1. Anticoagulation: Offer if CHA2DS2-VASc ≥ 2 (Consider if 1 in men). 1st-line: DOAC (e.g. Apixaban 5mg bd or Edoxaban 60mg OD).
2. Note: Do not offer Aspirin for stroke prevention in AF.
3. Bleeding Risk: Assess using ORBIT (preferred) or HAS-BLED. Address reversible risks (HTN, alcohol, NSAIDs). NICE NG196.

options.label: Rate Control (Standard)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Beta-blocker (e.g. Bisoprolol 2.5-10mg) or CCB (e.g. Diltiazem). Target HR < 90bpm at rest (or < 110bpm if sedentary).
2. Digoxin: Only as add-on if HR not controlled or in sedentary elderly. NICE NG196.

options.label: Rhythm Control (Specialist)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer for Cardioversion or Ablation if: Symptomatic despite rate control, young, first-onset AF, or HF suspected/caused by AF.
2. Meds: Flecainide (if no structural heart disease) or Amiodarone. NICE NG196.

tools.title: Ambulatory BP monitoring
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: When & how
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use to confirm hypertension (clinic BP 140/90+), white-coat effect, or resistant hypertension. Minimum 14 readings daytime, 7 night.
2. Interpret using ABPM thresholds (e.g. daytime ≥135/85). NICE NG136, CKS.

tools.title: Angina – nitrates
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Anti-anginal Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCP/BCS):
1. Acute: GTN Spray (1-2 puffs prn).
2. Preventative: First-line Beta-blocker (Bisoprolol) or CCB (Amlodipine). Titrate to maximum tolerated dose.
3. Secondary Prevention: Aspirin 75mg + Atorvastatin 80mg + ACEi (if diabetic/HTN).
4. Referral: Urgent referral to Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic (RACPC) for CTCA (CT Coronary Angiography). NICE NG72.

options.label: DAPT duration
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Post-ACS: DAPT 12 months then single antiplatelet (usually clopidogrel). Consider longer if high ischaemic risk.
2. Post PCI: As per stent type and bleeding risk. NICE NG185.

tools.title: Back to basics  heart sounds and cardiac examination – Management
tools.evidence: And this includes a whole string of interactive and informative webinars designed to address the primary care challenges of diagnosing and managing chronic conditions across a range of therapeutic areas. Today in this podcast we're going to be discussing an important part of the …

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indications: Murmur with red flags, suspected HF (BNP raised), syncope, embolic event, suspected valve disease.
2. Urgent: Suspected endocarditis, acute severe regurgitation. NICE NG208, CKS.

options.label: Follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Repeat echo per cardiology/serial findings. Treat HF, AF, hypertension per guidelines. NICE NG106, NG208.

tools.title: BNP – when to request
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Raised BNP
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NT-proBNP >2000: Urgent echo/specialist within 2 weeks. 400–2000: Routine within 6 weeks.
2. Baseline ECG, U&E, FBC, LFT, lipids. NICE NG106.

tools.title: Bradycardia – when to pace
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: ST elevation / acute
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency 999; aspirin 300 mg. Do not delay for repeat ECG in primary care. NICE NG185.

options.label: BBB / bradycardia / Long QT / Brugada
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer cardiology for pacemaker/ICD assessment if symptomatic or high risk.
2. Avoid QT-prolonging drugs if Long QT. NICE NG203, CKS.

tools.title: Cardiac arrest – survivor
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Post-resuscitation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Echo, coronary assessment; treat reversible cause. ICD if LVEF ≤35% or high-risk arrhythmia. Cardiac rehab.
2. Driving: Group 1 disqualified until specialist clearance; Group 2 6–12 months. NICE NG185, DVLA.

tools.title: Cardiac rehabilitation referral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Post-MI, post-CABG/PCI, HF, stable angina: Refer to cardiac rehab (exercise, education, psychological support).
2. Early referral post-discharge. NICE NG106, NG172.

tools.title: Cardiac sarcoid
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Suspected myocarditis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit if acute (ECG, troponin, echo). Avoid NSAIDs in acute phase. Long-term: HF treatment; avoid strenuous exercise until reviewed.
2. Takotsubo: Supportive; echo to confirm; usually recovers. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Cardiomyopathy – referral
tools.evidence: NICE NG106: NT-proBNP for diagnosis; echo for type. HFrEF: four pillars (ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i); diuretic for congestion. HFpEF: diuresis, empagliflozin, BP control.

options.label: Suspected (NT-proBNP > 400 pg/ml)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NT-proBNP > 2000: Urgent Specialist Assessment + Echo within 2 weeks.
2. NT-proBNP 400-2000: Routine Specialist Assessment + Echo within 6 weeks.
3. Baseline: 12-lead ECG, CXR, U&E, LFT, FBC, Iron Studies (exclude iron deficiency). NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFrEF (LVEF ≤ 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Initiate 'Four Pillars' simultaneously or in rapid sequence.
2. Diuretics: Furosemide or Bumetanide titrated to euphovolemia.
3. Cardiac Rehab: Mandatory referral. NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFpEF (LVEF > 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diuresis to symptoms.
2. Empagliflozin 10mg OD (NICE TA798) to reduce CV death/hospitalization risk.
3. Strict BP control (Target < 130/80). NICE NG106.

options.label: Exacerbation / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Acute: Double diuretic; consider IV if severe. Check U&E, BNP. Treat precipitant (AF, infection, non-adherence).
2. Admit: Severe breathlessness, hypoxia, hypotension, acute kidney injury, or poor response. NICE NG106, CKS.

options.label: 1: ACEi/ARB or ARNI
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line ACEi (Ramipril). If symptomatic on ACEi/ARB, switch to Sacubitril/Valsartan (ENTRESTO).
2. Monitoring: BP and U&E after each dose escalation. NICE NG106.

options.label: 2: Beta-Blocker (Bisoprolol/Carvedilol)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Start only when clinically stable. 'Start low, go slow'.
2. Target: Beta-blockade until heart rate 50-60 bpm if tolerated. NICE NG106.

options.label: 3: MRA (Spironolactone/Eplerenone)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: NYHA Class II-IV symptoms.
2. Review: mandatory K+ check at 1, 4, 8, and 12 weeks. NICE NG106.

options.label: 4: SGLT2 Inhibitor (Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Add 10mg OD regardless of diabetic status. Significant mortality benefit. NICE NG106.

tools.title: Chest pain – acute
tools.evidence: NICE NG72 (stable angina, CTCA), NG185 (acute coronary syndrome). Exclude ACS before attributing to musculoskeletal or GORD.

options.label: Stable / likely angina
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GTN prn; beta-blocker or CCB. Secondary prevention: aspirin, statin, ACEi if indicated.
2. Refer: Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic for CTCA. NICE NG72.

options.label: Acute / possible ACS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999; aspirin 300 mg if no contraindication.
2. Do not delay for troponin in primary care if typical presentation. NICE NG185.

options.label: Non-cardiac / musculoskeletal
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude cardiac cause (ECG, troponin if indicated). Consider costochondritis, muscle strain, Tietze's; NSAID/analgesia; reassurance.
2. If GORD/reflux: trial PPI. If anxiety: support and exclude organic cause first. NICE NG72, CKS.

options.label: Safety net
options.guidance: SAFETY: Reattend if central/crushing pain, breathlessness, collapse, or pain at rest. If suspected ACS call 999. NICE NG72, NG185.

tools.title: CVD risk – QRISK3
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Primary prevention, QRISK3 ≥10%
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Offer atorvastatin 20 mg (or simvastatin 40 mg if atorvastatin not tolerated). Discuss lifestyle. Recheck lipids in 3 months. NICE NG238.

options.label: Primary prevention, high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider higher intensity (atorvastatin 80 mg) if QRISK3 ≥10% and lifestyle addressed. NICE NG238.

options.label: Secondary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg). Aim LDL reduction >40%. Add ezetimibe if not at target. NICE NG238.

tools.title: DVT – anticoagulation duration
tools.evidence: NICE NG158: Wells score for DVT/PE; D-dimer (age-adjusted if >50). Imaging within 4h if likely DVT; CTPA for PE. DOAC 3 months minimum; extend if unprovoked or high risk.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:

tools.title: Endocarditis – prophylaxis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: NICE NG64
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antibiotic prophylaxis NOT routinely recommended for dental or GI/GU procedures.
2. Only consider for highest-risk patients (prosthetic valve, previous endocarditis, cyanotic congenital heart disease) having dental at site of infection. NICE NG64.

tools.title: Heart failure – device therapy
tools.evidence: NICE NG106: NT-proBNP for diagnosis; echo for type. HFrEF: four pillars (ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i); diuretic for congestion. HFpEF: diuresis, empagliflozin, BP control.

options.label: Suspected (NT-proBNP > 400 pg/ml)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NT-proBNP > 2000: Urgent Specialist Assessment + Echo within 2 weeks.
2. NT-proBNP 400-2000: Routine Specialist Assessment + Echo within 6 weeks.
3. Baseline: 12-lead ECG, CXR, U&E, LFT, FBC, Iron Studies (exclude iron deficiency). NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFrEF (LVEF ≤ 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Initiate 'Four Pillars' simultaneously or in rapid sequence.
2. Diuretics: Furosemide or Bumetanide titrated to euphovolemia.
3. Cardiac Rehab: Mandatory referral. NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFpEF (LVEF > 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diuresis to symptoms.
2. Empagliflozin 10mg OD (NICE TA798) to reduce CV death/hospitalization risk.
3. Strict BP control (Target < 130/80). NICE NG106.

options.label: Exacerbation / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Acute: Double diuretic; consider IV if severe. Check U&E, BNP. Treat precipitant (AF, infection, non-adherence).
2. Admit: Severe breathlessness, hypoxia, hypotension, acute kidney injury, or poor response. NICE NG106, CKS.

options.label: 1: ACEi/ARB or ARNI
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line ACEi (Ramipril). If symptomatic on ACEi/ARB, switch to Sacubitril/Valsartan (ENTRESTO).
2. Monitoring: BP and U&E after each dose escalation. NICE NG106.

options.label: 2: Beta-Blocker (Bisoprolol/Carvedilol)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Start only when clinically stable. 'Start low, go slow'.
2. Target: Beta-blockade until heart rate 50-60 bpm if tolerated. NICE NG106.

options.label: 3: MRA (Spironolactone/Eplerenone)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: NYHA Class II-IV symptoms.
2. Review: mandatory K+ check at 1, 4, 8, and 12 weeks. NICE NG106.

options.label: 4: SGLT2 Inhibitor (Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Add 10mg OD regardless of diabetic status. Significant mortality benefit. NICE NG106.

tools.title: Heart valve disease in adults  an update from NICE – Management
tools.evidence: Now for the next few episodes of the podcast, we've got something a little different for you. The webinars, which are being run in association with [Organisation], are

options.label: Severe / symptomatic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer cardiology/valve clinic. Echo for severity and LV function.
2. Endocarditis prophylaxis: only for high-risk procedures per NICE NG64.

options.label: Mild / surveillance
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Repeat echo per local protocol (often 1–2 years). Treat HF and AF per guidelines. NICE NG208.

tools.title: Hyperlipidaemia – familial
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Primary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. QRISK3 ≥10%: Atorvastatin 20 mg; consider 80 mg if high risk. Recheck lipids at 3 months.
2. Target: LDL-C reduction >40%. NICE CG181.

options.label: FH / familial
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer lipid clinic if Simon Broome criteria. Statin from childhood in FH. NICE CG71.

tools.title: Hypertension – first-line drug choice
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).

tools.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
tools.evidence: NICE NG106: NT-proBNP for diagnosis; echo for type. HFrEF: four pillars (ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i); diuretic for congestion. HFpEF: diuresis, empagliflozin, BP control.

options.label: Suspected (NT-proBNP > 400 pg/ml)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NT-proBNP > 2000: Urgent Specialist Assessment + Echo within 2 weeks.
2. NT-proBNP 400-2000: Routine Specialist Assessment + Echo within 6 weeks.
3. Baseline: 12-lead ECG, CXR, U&E, LFT, FBC, Iron Studies (exclude iron deficiency). NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFrEF (LVEF ≤ 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Initiate 'Four Pillars' simultaneously or in rapid sequence.
2. Diuretics: Furosemide or Bumetanide titrated to euphovolemia.
3. Cardiac Rehab: Mandatory referral. NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFpEF (LVEF > 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diuresis to symptoms.
2. Empagliflozin 10mg OD (NICE TA798) to reduce CV death/hospitalization risk.
3. Strict BP control (Target < 130/80). NICE NG106.

options.label: Exacerbation / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Acute: Double diuretic; consider IV if severe. Check U&E, BNP. Treat precipitant (AF, infection, non-adherence).
2. Admit: Severe breathlessness, hypoxia, hypotension, acute kidney injury, or poor response. NICE NG106, CKS.

options.label: 1: ACEi/ARB or ARNI
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line ACEi (Ramipril). If symptomatic on ACEi/ARB, switch to Sacubitril/Valsartan (ENTRESTO).
2. Monitoring: BP and U&E after each dose escalation. NICE NG106.

options.label: 2: Beta-Blocker (Bisoprolol/Carvedilol)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Start only when clinically stable. 'Start low, go slow'.
2. Target: Beta-blockade until heart rate 50-60 bpm if tolerated. NICE NG106.

options.label: 3: MRA (Spironolactone/Eplerenone)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: NYHA Class II-IV symptoms.
2. Review: mandatory K+ check at 1, 4, 8, and 12 weeks. NICE NG106.

options.label: 4: SGLT2 Inhibitor (Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Add 10mg OD regardless of diabetic status. Significant mortality benefit. NICE NG106.

tools.title: ICD – follow-up
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Usually led by cardiology/device clinic. Primary care: monitor for infection, ensure anticoagulation/rate control as indicated.
2. Driving: DVLA rules apply (group 1/2). NICE NG106, CKS.

tools.title: Lipid – familial hypercholesterolaemia
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Primary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. QRISK3 ≥10%: Atorvastatin 20 mg; consider 80 mg if high risk. Recheck lipids at 3 months.
2. Target: LDL-C reduction >40%. NICE CG181.

options.label: FH / familial
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer lipid clinic if Simon Broome criteria. Statin from childhood in FH. NICE CG71.

tools.title: Long QT
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: ST elevation / acute
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency 999; aspirin 300 mg. Do not delay for repeat ECG in primary care. NICE NG185.

options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer cardiology for pacemaker/ICD assessment if symptomatic or high risk.
2. Avoid QT-prolonging drugs if Long QT. NICE NG203, CKS.

tools.title: Lymphoedema
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Primary care & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Compression; skin care; exercise. Exclude venous/renal/cardiac cause.
2. Refer lymphoedema service if significant or secondary to cancer treatment. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Mitral regurgitation
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Severe / symptomatic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer cardiology/valve clinic. Echo for severity and LV function.
2. Endocarditis prophylaxis: only for high-risk procedures per NICE NG64.

options.label: Mild / surveillance
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Repeat echo per local protocol (often 1–2 years). Treat HF and AF per guidelines. NICE NG208.

tools.evidence: Palpitations in primary care: when to worry. Key points. Palpitations are a common presentation. First, take a history—regular or irregular, duration, triggers. Consider anxiety and mental health overlap; many patients have both cardiac concerns and anxiety. If red flags—syncope,…

tools.title: PE – thrombolysis
tools.evidence: NICE NG158: Wells score for DVT/PE; D-dimer (age-adjusted if >50). Imaging within 4h if likely DVT; CTPA for PE. DOAC 3 months minimum; extend if unprovoked or high risk.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):
1. Action: Urgent Proximal Leg US within 4h (or interim anticoagulation if wait >4h).
2. Result: If US negative but D-dimer positive, repeat US in 6-8 days.

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Immediate: CTPA (Computed Tomographic Pulmonary Angiography). Interim anticoagulation (e.g. Apixaban 10mg bd) if scan delayed >1h.
2. V/Q Scan: Preferred if renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe allergy to contrast.
3. Note: If PE likely, assess PESI score for suitability of outpatient management.

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).
2. Refer: Anticoagulation failure, thrombophilia testing (young, family history), cancer-associated. NICE NG158.

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 months (provoked/low risk), 6 months+ or indefinite (unprovoked or recurrence). NICE NG158.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

tools.title: Pericarditis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Acute idiopathic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NSAID (ibuprofen 400 mg tds) + PPI for 1–2 weeks. Colchicine 500 mcg bd can reduce recurrence.
2. Avoid steroids first-line. Rest from strenuous activity.
3. Refer: Large effusion, tamponade, failure to improve. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Peripheral arterial disease
tools.evidence: Management per NG147 and CKS PAD.

options.label: Medical management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antiplatelet (clopidogrel 75 mg or aspirin). Statin. Treat BP and diabetes. Supervised exercise.
2. Refer vascular if limiting symptoms or critical ischaemia. NICE NG147.

tools.title: Post-MI – secondary prevention
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antiplatelet: Aspirin 75 mg or clopidogrel 75 mg (DAPT duration per cardiology). Statin: atorvastatin 80 mg. Beta-blocker, ACEi/ARNI titrated. Cardiac rehab referral.
2. BP target <140/90; HbA1c if diabetic. Lifestyle: smoking, diet, activity. NICE NG185, NG106, NG172.

tools.title: Post-stroke – BP target
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: BP target & secondary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. BP: Target <130/80 if feasible (or <140/90). Antiplatelet: clopidogrel 75 mg or aspirin. Statin: atorvastatin 80 mg. AF: anticoagulate (DOAC).
2. Treat diabetes, smoking cessation. Swallow screen; rehab. NICE NG128, NG217.

tools.title: Primary prevention of cardiovascular disease  what has changed in QRISK3 and why – Management
tools.evidence: In other words, in patients with no evidence of established cardiovascular disease, no history of heart attack, stroke, TIA and JINAR or peripheral vasodosies. But of course, patients with these comorbidities are automatically at high cardiovascular risk. And we'll also highlight…

options.label: Primary prevention, QRISK3 ≥10%
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Offer atorvastatin 20 mg (or simvastatin 40 mg if atorvastatin not tolerated). Discuss lifestyle. Recheck lipids in 3 months. NICE NG238.

options.label: Primary prevention, high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider higher intensity (atorvastatin 80 mg) if QRISK3 ≥10% and lifestyle addressed. NICE NG238.

options.label: Secondary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg). Aim LDL reduction >40%. Add ezetimibe if not at target. NICE NG238.

tools.title: Raynaud's
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Primary
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; avoid cold; gloves. Nifedipine MR 10–20 mg bd if disabling. Screen for connective tissue disease (ANA, nailfold capillaroscopy) if secondary suspected.
2. Refer rheumatology if secondary or digital ulceration. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Stable angina management
tools.evidence: Management per NG126 and CKS Angina.

options.label: Anti-anginal Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCP/BCS):
1. Acute: GTN Spray (1-2 puffs prn).
2. Preventative: First-line Beta-blocker (Bisoprolol) or CCB (Amlodipine). Titrate to maximum tolerated dose.
3. Secondary Prevention: Aspirin 75mg + Atorvastatin 80mg + ACEi (if diabetic/HTN).
4. Referral: Urgent referral to Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic (RACPC) for CTCA (CT Coronary Angiography). NICE NG72.

options.label: Suspected myocarditis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

2. Takotsubo: Supportive; echo to confirm; usually recovers. NICE CKS.

tools.title: The overlap between COPD and heart disease – Management
tools.evidence: The overlap between COPD and heart disease. Patients with COPD often have cardiovascular comorbidity. Breathlessness may be pulmonary, cardiac, or both. Assess for heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. Use QRISK and consider statins; manage blood pressu…

options.label: LAMA+LABA (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. First-line for patients with persistent breathlessness or exacerbations despite SABA/LAMA mono.
2. Inhalers: e.g. Anoro Ellipta, Ultibro Breezhaler, Spiolto Respimat.
3. Action: Check technique; offer Pulmonary Rehab if MRC ≥ 2. NICE NG115.

options.label: Triple Therapy (LABA+LAMA+ICS)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Indication: Blood eosinophil count ≥ 0.3 x10^9/L OR ≥ 1 severe / 2 moderate exacerbations per year.
2. Inhalers: Trelegy Ellipta or Trimbow.
3. Risk: Discuss increased risk of pneumonia with ICS use. NICE NG115.

options.label: Refractory / Advanced COPD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Macrolide: Consider Azithromycin 250mg tiw if non-smoker and frequent exacerbations (requires baseline ECG & LFT).
2. Oxygen: Assess for LTOT (Long Term Oxygen Therapy) if pO2 < 7.3 kPa stable.
3. Referral: Lung volume reduction or Transplant assessment. NICE NG115.

options.label: Exacerbation / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Moderate: Increase SABA; add prednisolone 30 mg 5–7 days; consider antibiotic if purulent sputum.
2. Admit: Severe (respiratory failure, confusion, cyanosis), or poor response. NICE NG115, CKS.

tools.title: Tricuspid regurgitation
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Severe / symptomatic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer cardiology/valve clinic. Echo for severity and LV function.
2. Endocarditis prophylaxis: only for high-risk procedures per NICE NG64.

options.label: Mild / surveillance
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Repeat echo per local protocol (often 1–2 years). Treat HF and AF per guidelines. NICE NG208.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Severe / symptomatic

tools.title: Varicose veins
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Conservative & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Compression hosiery; leg elevation; weight loss if overweight.
2. Refer if symptomatic, skin changes, or patient choice after conservative trial. NICE CG168.

tools.title: Venous ulcer – compression
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Suspected Microbial Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IMMEDIATE: Emergency Same-Day Ophthalmology referral (A&E eye clinic).
2. First Aid: Stop contact lens wear immediately; do not patch the eye.
3. Note: High risk of permanent vision loss/perforation within 24-48h if untreated. Moorfields Guidelines.

tools.title: Ventricular ectopics
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Assessment & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. If symptomatic or frequent: ECG, echo; exclude structural heart disease and channelopathy. Reduce stimulants; treat anxiety if relevant.
2. Refer if structural disease, sustained VT, or very frequent. Beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker for symptoms. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Suspected Parkinson's
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG71):
1. Presentation: Asymmetrical resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia (slowness of movement).
2. Action: Urgent referral to Neurology or Elderly Care Specialist (within 6 weeks, untreated).
3. Note: Do not start Levodopa or other medications in primary care before specialist diagnosis.

tools.title: Abscess – skin
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Small / fluctuant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Incision and drainage; send pus if recurrent or cellulitis. Do not use antibiotic alone for uncomplicated abscess.
2. Consider flucloxacillin if cellulitis or systemic symptoms. NICE NG141.

options.label: Recurrent boils
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hygiene; nasal decolonisation (mupirocin) if nasal carriage. Screen household. Consider referral if persistent. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Acne – isotretinoin referral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild (comedones)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Topical: adapalene 0.1% or benzoyl peroxide 5% OD. If inadequate after 12 weeks add topical antibiotic (e.g. clindamycin). NICE NG198.

options.label: Moderate (inflammatory)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Fixed combination: adapalene + benzoyl peroxide, or topical abx + benzoyl peroxide. If inadequate: oral doxycycline 100 mg OD 12 weeks (or lymecycline). NICE NG198.

options.label: Severe or scarring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer dermatology for oral isotretinoin. Exclude pregnancy; contraception. Do not offer oral antibiotic long-term as monotherapy. NICE NG198.

options.label: When to refer / pregnancy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Severe, scarring, or failed oral antibiotic. Isotretinoin: pregnancy prevention programme; two forms contraception.
2. Pregnancy: Topical only; avoid oral tetracyclines, isotretinoin. Azithromycin if needed. NICE NG198.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild / Single lesion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical: Diclofenac 3% gel (Solaraze) twice daily for 60-90 days.
2. Cryotherapy: Consider if single, well-defined lesion.
3. Sun Protection: High SPF broad-spectrum sunscreen. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate / Field change (>5 lesions)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical First-line: Fluorouracil 5% cream (Efudix) once daily for 3-4 weeks. Warn patient of expected inflammatory 'crusting' reaction.
2. Alternative: Imiquimod 5% cream (Aldara) 3 times weekly for 4 weeks (review then repeat as needed).
3. Warning: If any lesion is painful, ulcerated, or growing, suspect SCC and refer 2WW. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Eczema – emollients
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Refractory Eczema / Psoriasis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Grade):
1. Phototherapy: Consider NB-UVB (Narrowband) 3 times weekly for 6-12 weeks if topical tx fails.
2. Systemic Non-biologics: Methotrexate (weekly), Ciclosporin (short-term), or Azathioprine. Requires baseline FBC, U&E, LFT, and Pro-collagen III peptide (for MTX).
3. Biologics (High impact): Dupilumab (Eczema) or Adalimumab/Ustekinumab (Psoriasis). Criteria: PASI > 10 and DLQI > 10 despite two systemic agents. NICE TA guidelines.

options.label: Pyoderma Gangrenosum / Vasculitis (Suspected)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Biopsy: Incisional biopsy (not punch) for histology and direct immunofluorescence (DIF).
2. First-line: High-dose Oral Prednisolone (0.5-1mg/kg) + steroid-sparing agent.
3. Triage: Urgent Dermatology review; exclude underlying IBD, Rheumatoid, or Myeloma. NICE CKS.

options.label: Eczema / dermatitis – when to refer

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Localised (Non-bullous)
options.guidance:

1. First-line: Hydrogen peroxide 1% cream (Crystacide) for 5 days.
2. Alternative: Topical fusidic acid 2% tds for 5 days (if peroxide unsuitable).
3. Hygiene: Crusts can be gently soaked off with warm water. NICE CKS.

options.label: Widespread or Bullous
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Oral Antibiotics: Flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 5 days (clarithromycin if allergic).
2. Bullous: Always use oral antibiotics as it is usually staphylococcal.
3. Hygiene: Handwashing, separate towels, avoid scratching. NICE CKS.

options.label: Exclusion / Contagion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. School/Work: Exclude until lesions are crusted and healed, OR 48 hours after starting antibiotics.
2. Recurrence: Consider nasal swab (MRSA?) and skin de-colonization. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Ingrowing toenail
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Conservative / Self-care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Soak foot: Warm salty water (10-15 mins, 3-4x daily).
2. Lifting nail: Gently lift nail edge with a clean wisp (if comfortable).
3. Footwear: Wear wide, comfortable shoes or sandals.
4. Nail care: Cut nails straight across, not too short at corners. NICE CKS.

options.label: Infected nail fold
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Check for spreading cellulitis or systemic symptoms.
2. Antibiotics: Flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 7 days (or clarithromycin).
3. Review: Review in 48-72h. If not improving, consider incision/drainage or specialist referral. NICE CKS.

options.label: Surgical referral (Podiatry)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Persistent pain, recurrent infection, or failure of conservative measures.
2. Procedure: Partial or total nail avulsion with phenolisation.
3. Referral: Refer to local podiatry or minor surgery clinic. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Paronychia
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Acute Paronychia (Bacterial)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Conservative: Warm saline soaks 3-4 times daily.
2. Topical: If minor, use topical antiseptic (Fucidin) or mupirocin.
3. Oral: If severe or cellulitis present, start flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 7 days (clarithromycin if penicillin-allergic).
4. Drainage: If abscess present, perform incision and drainage.
5. Safety-net: Return if fever, spreading redness, or no change in 48h. NICE CKS.

options.label: Chronic Paronychia (>6 weeks)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Protection: Avoid moisture/irritants; use cotton-lined gloves for wet work.
2. Topical: Use topical steroid (e.g. hydrocortisone / Betnovate) and/or topical antifungal (clotrimazole).
3. Hygiene: Keep area dry; avoid nail-biting.
4. Review: Primary care review in 4-6 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: General / Skin Care

2. Sunscreen: Use broad-spectrum high SPF daily.

options.guidance:

2. Alternative: Topical azelaic acid 15% gel bd.
3. Duration: Trial for 8-12 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: Oral treatment (Moderate/Severe)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: More severe disease or failure of topical therapy.
2. Medication: Oxytetracycline 500mg bd, OR Doxycycline 100mg od (or 40mg modified-release).
3. Course: 6-12 weeks initially. NICE CKS.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pyoderma gangrenosum: wound care; often need systemic treatment – refer dermatology. Dermatitis herpetiformis: gluten-free; dapsone if needed – refer. Dermatomyositis/Lupus/Scleroderma: refer rheumatology/dermatology.
2. Hirsutism: treat underlying (PCOS); cosmetic options. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Scalp (Adult)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Medicated Shampoo: Ketoconazole 2% (Nizoral) or coal tar based (Alphosyl/Capasal) twice weekly for 2-4 weeks.
2. Inflammation: If severe itch/redness, use moderate potency topical steroid application (e.g. Eumovate scalp) for up to 4 weeks.
3. Maintenance: Use medicated shampoo once weekly/fortnightly as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: Face and Body
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antifungal: Topical ketoconazole 2% cream or miconazole once or twice daily for 2-4 weeks.
2. Steroid: If inflamed, use mild topical steroid (e.g. Hydrocortisone 1%) for short course (max 2 weeks).
3. Hygiene: Use soap substitute; avoid greasy ointments. NICE CKS.

options.label: Cradle Cap (Infant)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Soften scale: Use baby oil, olive oil, or coconut oil to soften crusts overnight.
2. Brush: Gently brush off scale with a soft brush or fine-toothed comb.
3. Wash: Use baby shampoo to wash hair. Safety-net: Return if spreading to face/flexures or looking infected. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Skin – drug eruption
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Erythema multiforme: often viral; supportive. Erythema nodosum: treat cause; NSAID. Stop culprit drug. SJS/TEN: emergency – admit; stop drug; supportive care.
2. Drug eruption: stop drug; antihistamine/moderate steroid if needed. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Solar keratosis – field change
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild / Single lesion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical: Diclofenac 3% gel (Solaraze) twice daily for 60-90 days.
2. Cryotherapy: Consider if single, well-defined lesion.
3. Sun Protection: High SPF broad-spectrum sunscreen. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate / Field change (>5 lesions)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical First-line: Fluorouracil 5% cream (Efudix) once daily for 3-4 weeks. Warn patient of expected inflammatory 'crusting' reaction.
2. Alternative: Imiquimod 5% cream (Aldara) 3 times weekly for 4 weeks (review then repeat as needed).
3. Warning: If any lesion is painful, ulcerated, or growing, suspect SCC and refer 2WW. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Squamous cell – in situ
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Vitiligo / granuloma annulare
options.guidance:

2. BCC/SCC in situ: refer per 2WW or local pathway. NICE CKS, NG12.

tools.title: ADHD – adults
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Treatment Philosophy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Goal**: Not 'normalcy', but 'functional alignment'. 
2. **Multimodal**: Medication (Stimulants) + Executive Function Coaching + Social adjustment.
3. **Biological**: Correcting fronto-striatal dopaminergic deficit. Medication provides the 'brakes' for the brain.
4. **Psycho-Social**: Reducing the 'shame cycle' associated with executive dysfunction. Occupational/Educational adjustments (reasonable adjustments) are essential.

options.label: Clinical Criteria
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DSM-5: 6/9 symptoms of Inattention and/or Hyperactivity-Impulsivity (5/9 for adults) in ≥2 settings, present before age 12.
2. ICD-11 (6A05): Persistent pattern (≥6 months) of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity across settings.

options.label: Referral Pathway
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Child: Refer to Community Paediatrics or CAMHS.
2. Adult: Specialist ADHD service referral. Document impact on work, relationships, and driving safety. NICE NG87.

options.label: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line for adults. Prodrug (decreased abuse potential).
2. Dose: 30mg-70mg. 
3. Side effects: Insomnia, increased BP, appetite suppression.

options.label: Methylphenidate (Choice of IR/ER)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line for children/young people. 
2. Brands: **Conserta XL** (22% IR/78% ER) or **Medikinet XL** (50% IR/50% ER). 
3. Shared Care: GP takes over prescribing only after stabilization (usually 3 months) under Specialist Protocol.

options.label: Non-Stimulants (Atomoxetine)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice if stimulants contraindicated or high risk of diversion/misuse.
2. Warning: Rare risk of severe liver injury and suicidal ideation.

tools.title: Agoraphobia
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Treatment Philosophy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Core Mechanism**: Maintaining factor is 'Avoidance'. Recovery requires systematic exposure to the feared stimulus.
2. **Therapy**: 1st-line is **Graded Exposure** or CBT. Goal is 'Habituation' (anxiety decreases with prolonged exposure).
3. **Biological**: Meds (SSRIs) are secondary; they reduce the physical intensity of fear but do not 'cure' the phobia without exposure. Avoid Benzos as they prevent habituation. NICE CG159.

options.label: Specific Phobias (e.g. Heights, Animals, Blood)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Graded Exposure therapy (In vivo exposure). 80-90% success rate.
2. Note: For blood-injection-injury phobia, use 'Applied Tension' to prevent fainting. NICE CG159.

options.label: Social Anxiety Disorder (Social Phobia)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Marked fear of social/performance situations.
2. 1st-line: Individual CBT (Clark & Wells or Heimberg models).
3. Meds: Escitalopram or Sertraline if CBT declined/unavailable. NICE CG159.

options.label: Agoraphobia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Fear of being in situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable.
2. Treatment: CBT + systematic exposure. Often co-occurs with Panic Disorder; treat the Panic Disorder core first. NICE CG113.

tools.title: Alcohol – dependence
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Holistic Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Stages of Change**: Identify where the patient is (Pre-contemplation to Maintenance).
2. **Harm Reduction**: Reducing units, switching to lower ABV, safe drinking intervals. 
3. **Biological**: Supervised detox if dependent (≥10 units/day or morning shakes) followed by anti-craving meds.
4. **Psychosocial**: Engagement with community services (AA, SMART Recovery) and addressing 'dual diagnosis' (co-morbid anxiety/depression).

options.label: Withdrawal Severity & Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Severity: 
   - Mild (CIWA <10): Supportive, vitamins only.
   - Mod/Severe (CIWA ≥10): Chlordiazepoxide regime.
2. **Wernicke's Triad**: Ophthalmoplegia, Ataxia, Confusion. 
3. **CRITICAL**: Give Pabrinex (Thiamine) BEFORE Glucose to prevent precipitating Wernicke's. NICE CG115.

options.label: Anti-Craving Pharmacotherapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Acamprosate**: 666mg tds. Start day 1 of abstinence.
2. **Naltrexone**: 50mg OD. Monitor LFTs.
3. **Disulfiram**: Specialist only. NICE CG115.

tools.title: Alcohol – detox
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Severity & management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Mild (CIWA <10): Supportive; thiamine if at risk. Mod/Severe (CIWA ≥10): Chlordiazepoxide reducing regime; Pabrinex (thiamine) BEFORE glucose.
2. Wernicke's: ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, confusion – emergency Pabrinex. Consider admission if severe. NICE CG115.

tools.title: Alcohol – harmful use
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Brief intervention; structured advice; follow-up. Address motivation; offer support (e.g. AA, SMART).
2. If escalating or not responding, refer to specialist. Exclude dependence (withdrawal, tolerance). NICE CG115.

options.label: Severity & management

tools.title: Anorexia – referral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Specialist Triage Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Dual-Track Care**: Simultaneous stabilization of medical risk (Refeeding/Cardiovascular) and intensive specialized psychotherapy.
2. **Biological**: Focus on electrolyte balance (K, PO4, Mg) and cardiac rhythm. Nutritional rehabilitation is the primary goal.
3. **Psychological**: Addressing the 'cognitive anorexic core' and body image distortion using specialized models (MANTRA/CBT-ED).
4. **Systemic**: Multi-disciplinary team (MDT) involvement is mandatory (Psychiatrist, Dietitian, Specialist Nurse).

options.label: Life-Threatening Markers
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cardiovascular: HR <40 bpm, SBP <90 mmHg, QTc prolongation.
2. Metabolic: K+ <3.0, Phosphate <0.5 (Refeeding risk), Glucose <3.0.
3. Physical: Temp <35.5°C, BMI <13. 
4. Action: Emergency admission to medical ward + specialist ED liaison.

options.label: Anorexia (Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: AN-top (Anorexia Nervosa Focused Psychotherapy), MANTRA (Maudsley Anorexia Nervosa Treatment for Adults), or CBT-ED.

options.label: Bulimia (Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: Bulimia-focused CBT (CBT-BN) or IPT.

tools.title: Anxiety – medication choice
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Anxiety / GAD / panic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CBT first-line; SSRI if preferred or moderate–severe. Benzodiazepines short-term only. Reduce gradually. NICE NG226, CKS.

options.label: Bipolar / psychosis / monitoring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lithium: check U&E, TFT, Ca; therapeutic level. Clozapine: FBC monitoring. Section 2/3: MHA process; inform rights. NICE NG222, NG10.

options.label: Eating / other
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Eating disorders: refer if suspected. Gambling/hoarding: signpost; consider referral. Delirium: treat cause; avoid antipsychotic unless distress. NICE NG69, CKS.

options.label: Crisis / when to section
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Risk: Assess suicide/self-harm and risk to others. Crisis team/section: MHA assessment if detention needed (Section 2/3). Inform patient of rights; nearest relative. 2. De-escalation; avoid coercion unless risk. NICE NG10, NG222, CKS.

tools.title: Autism – adult
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Ethos**: Transition from a 'medical model' (fixing deficits) to a 'social model' (adjusting environment).
2. **Co-morbidity**: High rates of ADHD, Anxiety, and Dyspraxia. Always screen for co-occurring conditions.
3. **Biological**: Meds have NO role in core ASD features. Used only for co-morbidities (e.g. Melatonin for sleep, SSRIs for OCD).
4. **Social**: Educational (EHCP) and Workplace adjustments are the primary interventions.

options.label: Child/Young Person
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Local multi-agency ASD pathway (Paediatrics/CAMHS).
2. Screening: SCQ (Social Communication Questionnaire). 
3. Assessment: ADOS and ADI-R (Gold standard tools).

options.label: Adult suspected ASD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Screening: **AQ-10** (Score ≥6 = Refer).
2. Referral: Specialist diagnostic assessment only if significant impact on social/working life. NICE CG142.

tools.title: Bereavement
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

tools.title: Beyond baby blues  supporting mental health in parents and partners – Management
tools.evidence: So welcome back everybody to the podcast. It gives me really great pleasure to welcome back Jenny Barnes who's going to be talking to us about perinatal mental health again. We had a really wonderful first podcast where we talked all about the impact of perinatal mental health, j…

options.label: Assessment & support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

tools.title: Bipolar – acute
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Philosophy of Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Safety First**: Immediate risk assessment for Bipolar/Psychosis. Intent to self-harm or harm others (delusional pull).
2. **Biological Core**: Mood stabilizers (Lithium) and Antipsychotics are non-negotiable for stability. High emphasis on medication adherence.
3. **Social/Rehab**: Early Intervention Services (EIP) focus on maintaining social roles (work/education) during the 'critical period' of the first 3 years.
4. **Long-term**: Prophylaxis to prevent 'kindling' (where each subsequent episode is easier to trigger and harder to treat). NICE CG185, CG178.

options.label: Acute Mania / Hypomania
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE CG185):
1. Stop: Antidepressants immediately.
2. 1st-line: Antipsychotic (Haloperidol, Olanzapine, Quetiapine, or Risperidone).
3. Failure: Trial 2nd antipsychotic. Lithium as 3rd-line in acute phase.
4. Type distinction: Bipolar I (Full mania, often requires admission); Bipolar II (Hypomania + Severe Depression).

options.label: Bipolar Depression
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choices: Quetiapine (monotherapy), Olanzapine + Fluoxetine, or Lamotrigine (titrate slowly to prevent SJS).
2. Avoid: Antidepressant monotherapy (risk of switch to mania). NICE CG185.

options.label: Maintenance (Lithium)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target Level: 0.6-1.0 mmol/L.
2. Monitoring: Levels q3m (initially q1w). TFT/U&E/Calcium q6m.
3. Toxicity: Coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, confusion. Emergency A&E. NICE CG185.

options.label: Early Intervention (EIP)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Mandatory within 24h of suspected First Episode Psychosis (FEP).
2. Pharmacology: Oral atypical antipsychotic (Aripiprazole or Risperidone low-dose). NICE CG178.

options.label: Treatment Resistant Schizophrenia (TRS)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of 2x antipsychotics (at least one 2nd-gen) for ≥6 weeks at optimal dose.
2. Clozapine: **The only evidence-based treatment for TRS**. Mandatory FBC monitoring (risk of agranulocytosis). Specialist initiation only. NICE CG178.

tools.title: Bipolar – depression
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Holistic Consultant Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Biological**: Antidepressants (SSRIs 1st-line) + optimize physical health (sleep/exercise/thyroid).
2. **Psychological**: Evidence-based CBT, IPT, or Psychodynamic therapy. Strategy is to change cognitive distorting loops.
3. **Social**: Stabilize housing, employment, and social isolation. Review significant relational stressors.
4. **Remission Goal**: Total symptomatic relief, not just improvement. Continue meds for 6-12 months post-recovery. NICE NG222.

options.label: MDD Diagnosis (DSM-5 / PHQ-9)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Core: ≥5 of 9 symptoms for ≥2 weeks. Must include Mood or Anhedonia.
2. Severity Stratification: 
   - Mild: PHQ-9 10-14. 
   - Moderate: PHQ-9 15-19.
   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

tools.title: Bulimia
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Specialist Triage Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Dual-Track Care**: Simultaneous stabilization of medical risk (Refeeding/Cardiovascular) and intensive specialized psychotherapy.
2. **Biological**: Focus on electrolyte balance (K, PO4, Mg) and cardiac rhythm. Nutritional rehabilitation is the primary goal.
3. **Psychological**: Addressing the 'cognitive anorexic core' and body image distortion using specialized models (MANTRA/CBT-ED).
4. **Systemic**: Multi-disciplinary team (MDT) involvement is mandatory (Psychiatrist, Dietitian, Specialist Nurse).

options.label: Life-Threatening Markers
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cardiovascular: HR <40 bpm, SBP <90 mmHg, QTc prolongation.
2. Metabolic: K+ <3.0, Phosphate <0.5 (Refeeding risk), Glucose <3.0.
3. Physical: Temp <35.5°C, BMI <13. 
4. Action: Emergency admission to medical ward + specialist ED liaison.

options.label: Anorexia (Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: AN-top (Anorexia Nervosa Focused Psychotherapy), MANTRA (Maudsley Anorexia Nervosa Treatment for Adults), or CBT-ED.

options.label: Bulimia (Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: Bulimia-focused CBT (CBT-BN) or IPT.

tools.title: Capacity – assessment
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess capacity per MCA: understand, retain, weigh, communicate. Decision-specific. Best interests if lacking capacity; involve family/IMCA.
2. DoLS/LPS if deprivation of liberty in care. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.guidance:

2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

options.label: Amber (Intermediate Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assessment: Check for focus (ears, urine, chest). Consider urine dip.
2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.label: Red (High Risk / Sepsis)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

options.label: Suspected ME/CFS

tools.title: Dementia – agitation
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Philosophy of Dementia Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Approach**: Person-centered care focusing on preserving dignity and functional independence.
2. **Biological**: Managing reversible factors (infection/nutrition) and carefully titrating specialized cognitive enhancers.
3. **Psychological**: Validation therapy and addressing 'met and unmet needs' underlying behavioral symptoms (BPSD).
4. **Social**: Essential focus on Carer Support (respite, benefits) and home safety assessments (Occupational Therapy).

options.label: Alzheimer's Disease (Commonest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Early episodic memory loss, word-finding difficulty.
2. Imaging: Medial temporal lobe atrophy.
3. Meds: AChE inhibitors (Donepezil) or NMDA antagonists (Memantine).

options.label: Vascular Dementia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Stepwise decline, focal neurological signs, executive dysfunction.
2. Management: Aggressive V-risk factor control (BP, Lipids, Diabetes, Antiplatelets).

options.label: Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triad: Visual hallucinations, Parkinsonism, Fluctuating cognition.
2. **CRITICAL WARNING**: Extreme sensitivity to antipsychotics (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome risk). Use Quetiapine or Clozapine with extreme caution if BPSD severe.

options.label: Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Personality change, disinhibition, hyperoriality, or language decline (Primary Progressive Aphasia).
2. Management: SSRIs (e.g. Paroxetine) for behavioral symptoms. AChE inhibitors may worsen agitation in FTD.

options.label: Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Step 1: Rule out delirium (UTI/Pain/Meds/Constipation/Dehydration).
2. Step 2: Non-pharmacological (Life story work, music therapy).
3. Step 3: Pharmacological (Risperidone 0.25-0.5mg max 6w). Consider Trazodone or Lorazepam for acute severe distress. NICE NG97.

options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Approach**: Person-centered care focusing on preserving dignity and functional independence.
2. **Biological**: Managing reversible factors (infection/nutrition) and carefully titrating specialized cognitive enhancers.
3. **Psychological**: Validation therapy and addressing 'met and unmet needs' underlying behavioral symptoms (BPSD).
4. **Social**: Essential focus on Carer Support (respite, benefits) and home safety assessments (Occupational Therapy).

options.label: Alzheimer's Disease (Commonest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Early episodic memory loss, word-finding difficulty.
2. Imaging: Medial temporal lobe atrophy.
3. Meds: AChE inhibitors (Donepezil) or NMDA antagonists (Memantine).

options.label: Vascular Dementia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Stepwise decline, focal neurological signs, executive dysfunction.
2. Management: Aggressive V-risk factor control (BP, Lipids, Diabetes, Antiplatelets).

options.label: Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triad: Visual hallucinations, Parkinsonism, Fluctuating cognition.
2. **CRITICAL WARNING**: Extreme sensitivity to antipsychotics (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome risk). Use Quetiapine or Clozapine with extreme caution if BPSD severe.

options.label: Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Personality change, disinhibition, hyperoriality, or language decline (Primary Progressive Aphasia).
2. Management: SSRIs (e.g. Paroxetine) for behavioral symptoms. AChE inhibitors may worsen agitation in FTD.

options.label: Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Step 1: Rule out delirium (UTI/Pain/Meds/Constipation/Dehydration).
2. Step 2: Non-pharmacological (Life story work, music therapy).
3. Step 3: Pharmacological (Risperidone 0.25-0.5mg max 6w). Consider Trazodone or Lorazepam for acute severe distress. NICE NG97.

tools.title: Depression – elderly
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Holistic Consultant Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Biological**: Antidepressants (SSRIs 1st-line) + optimize physical health (sleep/exercise/thyroid).
2. **Psychological**: Evidence-based CBT, IPT, or Psychodynamic therapy. Strategy is to change cognitive distorting loops.
3. **Social**: Stabilize housing, employment, and social isolation. Review significant relational stressors.
4. **Remission Goal**: Total symptomatic relief, not just improvement. Continue meds for 6-12 months post-recovery. NICE NG222.

options.label: MDD Diagnosis (DSM-5 / PHQ-9)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Core: ≥5 of 9 symptoms for ≥2 weeks. Must include Mood or Anhedonia.
2. Severity Stratification: 
   - Mild: PHQ-9 10-14. 
   - Moderate: PHQ-9 15-19.
   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

tools.title: Insomnia – CBT
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Sleep Specialist Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Principle**: Distinguish between Primary Insomnia and secondary to comorbidities (Pain/OSA/Depression).
2. **Therapy**: **CBT-I is the gold standard 1st-line treatment**—superior long-term results to pharmacological options.
3. **Biological**: Circadian rhythm stabilization (melatonin) and conservative use of sedative hypnotics for short-term relief only.
4. **Environment**: Optimization of the sleep environment and addressing 'sleep effort' (the paradoxical anxiety about falling asleep).

options.label: Behavioural Interventions
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Sleep Restriction**: Limit time in bed to actual sleep duration (min 5h). Increases 'sleep drive'.
2. **Stimulus Control**: Leave bed if awake for >20 mins. Re-associate bed with sleep only.
3. **Cognitive**: Challenging 'catastrophic' thoughts about sleep loss impact.

1. **Philosophy**: Shift from 'Is it physical OR mental?' to 'How is the nervous system communicating distress?'.
2. **Validation**: Acknowledge symptoms are REAL (not 'it's all in your head').
3. **Mechanism**: Dysregulation of the autonomic nervous system or 'top-down' sensory processing errors (FND).
4. **Goal**: Manage symptoms and improve function rather than 'eliminating' the sensation.

options.label: Functional Neurological Disorder (FND)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Based on *positive signs* (e.g. Hoover's sign for leg weakness), not just exclusion.
2. Therapy: Specialized Physiotherapy (re-training movement) + CBT focused on symptom retraining.
3. Meds: Low-dose TCAs (Amitriptyline) for co-morbid pain/sleep.

options.label: Somatisation / MUS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Schedule: Regular 15-min appointments (regardless of symptom flare) to reduce 'crisis-driven' care.
2. Education: Use metaphors (e.g. 'Software vs Hardware' problem).
3. Meds: SSRIs if significant co-morbid anxiety/depression.

options.label: Support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Acknowledge stress; signpost to IAPT, crisis lines. Treat depression/anxiety per NICE.
2. Safety-net: risk assessment. NICE NG222, NG226.

tools.title: Mixed anxiety and depression
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Holistic Consultant Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Biological**: Antidepressants (SSRIs 1st-line) + optimize physical health (sleep/exercise/thyroid).
2. **Psychological**: Evidence-based CBT, IPT, or Psychodynamic therapy. Strategy is to change cognitive distorting loops.
3. **Social**: Stabilize housing, employment, and social isolation. Review significant relational stressors.
4. **Remission Goal**: Total symptomatic relief, not just improvement. Continue meds for 6-12 months post-recovery. NICE NG222.

options.label: MDD Diagnosis (DSM-5 / PHQ-9)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Core: ≥5 of 9 symptoms for ≥2 weeks. Must include Mood or Anhedonia.
2. Severity Stratification: 
   - Mild: PHQ-9 10-14. 
   - Moderate: PHQ-9 15-19.
   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

tools.title: Obsessive–compulsive disorder – Management
tools.evidence: (Intro removed; no clinical content in this segment.)

options.label: Consultant Strategic Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **PTSD Philosophy**: Focus on 're-processing' traumatic memories rather than avoidance. 
2. **OCD Philosophy**: Focus on 'Exposure & Response Prevention' (ERP). Breaking the link between obsession and neutralizing compulsion.
3. **Meds**: SSRIs/SNRIs used primarily to 'quieten' the cognitive noise, facilitating engagement in intensive therapy. NICE NG116, CG31.

options.label: PTSD Evidence-Based Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Re-experiencing (flashbacks), avoidance, and hyperarousal >1 month post-trauma.
2. 1st-line: **Trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT)** or **EMDR** (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing).
3. Meds: Venlafaxine or SSRI (Sertraline) only if patient prefers or therapy failed. Do NOT use Benzos. NICE NG116.

options.label: Complex PTSD (C-PTSD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Core PTSD + disturbances in self-organization (affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, relational diffs).
2. Management: Requires longer-term stabilization phase followed by trauma-focused work. NICE NG116.

options.label: OCD Stepwise Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: **ERP** (Exposure & Response Prevention) +/- SSRI.
2. Meds: Often require higher doses (e.g., Fluoxetine 60-80mg, Sertraline 200mg). Trial for ≥12 weeks.
3. Resistance: Consider adding Clomipramine (TCA) or an atypical antipsychotic adjunct. NICE CG31.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Priority**: Reduce fatalities (Overdose prevention).
2. **Assessment**: Frequency, route (IV risk), cost, and criminal justice involvement.
3. **Dual Diagnosis**: High correlation with trauma (PTSD) and EUPD. Treat co-morbidities simultaneously.

options.label: Opioid Dependence (Heroin/Methadone)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. OAT: Opioid Agonist Treatment (Methadone or Buprenorphine) is the standard of care.
2. Safety: Provide Naloxone kits for home use. Screening for Hep C and HIV.

options.label: Cannabis/Cocaine
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Psychosocial (CBT, Motivational Interviewing, Contingency Management).
2. Meds: No licensed maintenance pharmacotherapy. Symptom management only.

tools.title: Perinatal mental health  awareness, risks and impacts – Management
tools.evidence: It gives me great pleasure to introduce you to [Name] who is a GP and Warwickshire and a perinatal mental health GP champion and today we're talking all about perinatal mental health. Welcome Jenny. Thanks very much James and thanks for having me on the podcast today. It's great …

options.label: Assessment & support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Screen for depression/anxiety; assess bonding, risk. Refer to specialist perinatal mental health if moderate–severe or at risk.
2. Meds: Review in pregnancy/breastfeeding (BUMPS). NICE NG192, CKS.

tools.title: Personality disorder – borderline
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Management Ethos
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Validation**: Acknowledge the intense emotional pain while maintaining clear clinical boundaries.
2. **Stability**: Long-term commitment to a single therapeutic model (DBT/MBTP). Avoid 'fragmented care' (seeing multiple different teams).
3. **Safety**: Risk is often chronic but fluctuating. Focus on 'Safety Planning' over 'Risk Assessment scores'.
4. **Medication**: Avoid polypharmacy. Use as sparse adjuncts for specific symptoms (sleep/arousal) ONLY.

options.label: DBT Components (Consultant Guide)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Goal: Build 'a life worth living'.
2. Modules: 
   - Mindfulness: Staying in the present.
   - Distress Tolerance: Crisis survival (TIPP: Temperature, Intense exercise, Paced breathing).
   - Emotion Regulation: Reducing vulnerability to 'emotion mind'.
   - Interpersonal Effectiveness: Assertiveness and boundary setting.

options.label: Approach to Self-Harm
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Strategy: Validate distress while maintaining boundaries. Avoid 'rescuing' behavior that reinforces maladaptive coping.
2. Pharmacotherapy: Use low-dose Quetiapine (25mg) or Promethazine ONLY for acute arousal, not long-term. NICE CG78.

tools.title: Phobia – social
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Treatment Philosophy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Core Mechanism**: Maintaining factor is 'Avoidance'. Recovery requires systematic exposure to the feared stimulus.
2. **Therapy**: 1st-line is **Graded Exposure** or CBT. Goal is 'Habituation' (anxiety decreases with prolonged exposure).
3. **Biological**: Meds (SSRIs) are secondary; they reduce the physical intensity of fear but do not 'cure' the phobia without exposure. Avoid Benzos as they prevent habituation. NICE CG159.

options.label: Specific Phobias (e.g. Heights, Animals, Blood)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Graded Exposure therapy (In vivo exposure). 80-90% success rate.
2. Note: For blood-injection-injury phobia, use 'Applied Tension' to prevent fainting. NICE CG159.

options.label: Social Anxiety Disorder (Social Phobia)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Marked fear of social/performance situations.
2. 1st-line: Individual CBT (Clark & Wells or Heimberg models).
3. Meds: Escitalopram or Sertraline if CBT declined/unavailable. NICE CG159.

options.label: Agoraphobia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Fear of being in situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable.
2. Treatment: CBT + systematic exposure. Often co-occurs with Panic Disorder; treat the Panic Disorder core first. NICE CG113.

tools.title: Psychosis – referral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Philosophy of Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Safety First**: Immediate risk assessment for Bipolar/Psychosis. Intent to self-harm or harm others (delusional pull).
2. **Biological Core**: Mood stabilizers (Lithium) and Antipsychotics are non-negotiable for stability. High emphasis on medication adherence.
3. **Social/Rehab**: Early Intervention Services (EIP) focus on maintaining social roles (work/education) during the 'critical period' of the first 3 years.
4. **Long-term**: Prophylaxis to prevent 'kindling' (where each subsequent episode is easier to trigger and harder to treat). NICE CG185, CG178.

options.label: Acute Mania / Hypomania
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE CG185):
1. Stop: Antidepressants immediately.
2. 1st-line: Antipsychotic (Haloperidol, Olanzapine, Quetiapine, or Risperidone).
3. Failure: Trial 2nd antipsychotic. Lithium as 3rd-line in acute phase.
4. Type distinction: Bipolar I (Full mania, often requires admission); Bipolar II (Hypomania + Severe Depression).

options.label: Bipolar Depression
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choices: Quetiapine (monotherapy), Olanzapine + Fluoxetine, or Lamotrigine (titrate slowly to prevent SJS).
2. Avoid: Antidepressant monotherapy (risk of switch to mania). NICE CG185.

options.label: Maintenance (Lithium)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target Level: 0.6-1.0 mmol/L.
2. Monitoring: Levels q3m (initially q1w). TFT/U&E/Calcium q6m.
3. Toxicity: Coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, confusion. Emergency A&E. NICE CG185.

options.label: Early Intervention (EIP)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Mandatory within 24h of suspected First Episode Psychosis (FEP).
2. Pharmacology: Oral atypical antipsychotic (Aripiprazole or Risperidone low-dose). NICE CG178.

options.label: Treatment Resistant Schizophrenia (TRS)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of 2x antipsychotics (at least one 2nd-gen) for ≥6 weeks at optimal dose.
2. Clozapine: **The only evidence-based treatment for TRS**. Mandatory FBC monitoring (risk of agranulocytosis). Specialist initiation only. NICE CG178.

1. Diagnosis: Re-experiencing (flashbacks), avoidance, and hyperarousal >1 month post-trauma.
2. 1st-line: **Trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT)** or **EMDR** (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing).
3. Meds: Venlafaxine or SSRI (Sertraline) only if patient prefers or therapy failed. Do NOT use Benzos. NICE NG116.

options.label: Complex PTSD (C-PTSD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Core PTSD + disturbances in self-organization (affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, relational diffs).
2. Management: Requires longer-term stabilization phase followed by trauma-focused work. NICE NG116.

options.label: OCD Stepwise Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: **ERP** (Exposure & Response Prevention) +/- SSRI.
2. Meds: Often require higher doses (e.g., Fluoxetine 60-80mg, Sertraline 200mg). Trial for ≥12 weeks.
3. Resistance: Consider adding Clomipramine (TCA) or an atypical antipsychotic adjunct. NICE CG31.

tools.title: Schizophrenia – first episode
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Philosophy of Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Safety First**: Immediate risk assessment for Bipolar/Psychosis. Intent to self-harm or harm others (delusional pull).
2. **Biological Core**: Mood stabilizers (Lithium) and Antipsychotics are non-negotiable for stability. High emphasis on medication adherence.
3. **Social/Rehab**: Early Intervention Services (EIP) focus on maintaining social roles (work/education) during the 'critical period' of the first 3 years.
4. **Long-term**: Prophylaxis to prevent 'kindling' (where each subsequent episode is easier to trigger and harder to treat). NICE CG185, CG178.

options.label: Acute Mania / Hypomania
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE CG185):
1. Stop: Antidepressants immediately.
2. 1st-line: Antipsychotic (Haloperidol, Olanzapine, Quetiapine, or Risperidone).
3. Failure: Trial 2nd antipsychotic. Lithium as 3rd-line in acute phase.
4. Type distinction: Bipolar I (Full mania, often requires admission); Bipolar II (Hypomania + Severe Depression).

options.label: Bipolar Depression
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choices: Quetiapine (monotherapy), Olanzapine + Fluoxetine, or Lamotrigine (titrate slowly to prevent SJS).
2. Avoid: Antidepressant monotherapy (risk of switch to mania). NICE CG185.

options.label: Maintenance (Lithium)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target Level: 0.6-1.0 mmol/L.
2. Monitoring: Levels q3m (initially q1w). TFT/U&E/Calcium q6m.
3. Toxicity: Coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, confusion. Emergency A&E. NICE CG185.

options.label: Early Intervention (EIP)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Mandatory within 24h of suspected First Episode Psychosis (FEP).
2. Pharmacology: Oral atypical antipsychotic (Aripiprazole or Risperidone low-dose). NICE CG178.

options.label: Treatment Resistant Schizophrenia (TRS)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of 2x antipsychotics (at least one 2nd-gen) for ≥6 weeks at optimal dose.
2. Clozapine: **The only evidence-based treatment for TRS**. Mandatory FBC monitoring (risk of agranulocytosis). Specialist initiation only. NICE CG178.

3. Referral: Emergency department if lethal act or active intent. Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) for persistent self-harm. NICE NG225.
