options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive: fluids, paracetamol/ibuprofen for discomfort. Usually self-limiting.
2. Refer if dehydration, meningism, or immunocompromised. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Head lice
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Head lice: wet combing or dimeticone/lotion (check resistance). Two applications 7 days apart. Pubic lice: permethrin or malathion; treat contacts.
2. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Headache – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: First-line: Stratified Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH Guidelines):
1. Combined Approach: Soluble Aspirin (900mg) or Naproxen (500mg) + Triptan (e.g. Sumatriptan 50-100mg) + Prokinetic Anti-emetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
2. Note: Treat early at onset of headache, not aura. Avoid opioids (risk of Medication Overuse Headache). NICE NG150.

options.label: Triptan Failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Switch: Trial different triptan or different formulation (e.g. Sumatriptan Nasal Spray or SC).
2. MOH: Review for Medication Overuse Headache if using triptans ≥ 10 days/month. NICE NG150.

options.label: Initial Choice (Indicated if ≥2 attacks/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH/RCP):
1. First-line choices: Propranolol (80-160mg), Amitriptyline (10-50mg nocte), or Topiramate (titrate to 50mg-100mg - warn about teratogenicity/birth control).
2. Second-line: Candesartan (8-16mg) - widely used by neurologists off-label but supported by evidence. NICE NG150.

options.label: Specialist Interventions (Consultant Care)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CGRP Monoclonals (e.g. Erenumab, Fremanezumab): Indicated if ≥4 migraine days/month and failure of 3 oral preventatives. NICE TA.
2. Botox: Protocolized 31-site injection (PREEMPT) if chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, 8 being migraine). NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: Red flags / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: Thunderclap (SAH), new sudden severe, fever + neck stiffness (meningitis), papilloedema.
2. Refer: New headache ≥50y, progressive, positional, or focal neurology. NICE NG150, NG51.

tools.title: Henoch-Schönlein
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Most cases self-limiting: supportive care, rest until symptoms resolve. Analgesia (paracetamol/ibuprofen) for joint/abdominal pain.
2. Monitor: BP, urinalysis (blood/protein), serum creatinine and electrolytes. Repeat urine at 1–2 weeks and after resolution (risk of nephritis).
3. Refer: Nephritis, severe abdominal pain, GI bleed, orchitis, or organ-threatening disease. Urgent if unwell or renal impairment. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Hypertension – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

tools.title: Hypospadias
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Circumcision: Not routinely recommended for physiological phimosis (resolves with time). If pathological phimosis or parental request after discussion: refer to paediatric surgery/urology.
2. Phimosis: Topical steroid (e.g. betamethasone 0.05% once daily for 4–8 weeks) if ballooning or infection; refer if failed or scarring. NICE CKS.
3. Hypospadias: Refer to paediatric urology (surgical correction). Do not circumcise before referral. NICE NG11, NG111, CKS.

tools.title: Hypothyroidism – congenital
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

tools.title: IBD – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: IBD / colitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IBD: refer; maintain on treatment per specialist. Microscopic colitis: consider budesonide. Rectal bleeding: FIT, sigmoidoscopy/colonoscopy per pathway.
2. NICE NG129, NG12.

options.label: Liver / rare
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Autoimmune hepatitis/PBC/PSC: refer hepatology. Haemochromatosis: venesection. Wilson's: refer. Gastroparesis: diet, prokinetic; refer. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Immunisation – catch-up
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use Green Book schedule; give at minimum intervals (4 weeks for inactivated; no need to restart). MMR, pre-school booster, HPV, MenACWY as per schedule.
2. Refer to immunisation clinic if complex or travel. NICE CKS, Green Book.

tools.title: Impetigo – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Localised (Non-bullous)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Hydrogen peroxide 1% cream (Crystacide) for 5 days.
2. Alternative: Topical fusidic acid 2% tds for 5 days (if peroxide unsuitable).
3. Hygiene: Crusts can be gently soaked off with warm water. NICE CKS.

options.label: Widespread or Bullous
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Oral Antibiotics: Flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 5 days (clarithromycin if allergic).
2. Bullous: Always use oral antibiotics as it is usually staphylococcal.
3. Hygiene: Handwashing, separate towels, avoid scratching. NICE CKS.

options.label: Exclusion / Contagion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. School/Work: Exclude until lesions are crusted and healed, OR 48 hours after starting antibiotics.
2. Recurrence: Consider nasal swab (MRSA?) and skin de-colonization. NICE CKS.

steps.question: Consultations for children with additional needs

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider communication needs, sensory environment, reasonable adjustments. Involve family and carers.
2. Use clear language; allow time; avoid assumptions. NICE NG76, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Signpost to local SEND and family support. Coordinate with education and social care where appropriate. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Inguinal hernia – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Green (Low Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Management: Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for distress (not for fever alone).
2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

options.label: Amber (Intermediate Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assessment: Check for focus (ears, urine, chest). Consider urine dip.
2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.label: Red (High Risk / Sepsis)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

tools.title: Jaundice – neonatal
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use NICE threshold graphs (gestational age, hours of life). Phototherapy or exchange if above threshold.
2. Refer if conjugated jaundice, prolonged, or unwell. Check TFTs if prolonged. NICE CG98, CKS.

tools.title: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: persistent joint swelling, morning stiffness, limp. Urgent paediatric rheumatology referral. NSAIDs for symptom relief.
2. DMARDs/biologics as per paediatric rheumatology. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Kawasaki
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: fever ≥5 days + rash, conjunctivitis, cracked lips, lymph nodes, palm/sole changes. Urgent paediatric referral.
2. IVIG + aspirin to reduce coronary aneurysm risk. Echocardiography. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Septic arthritis/osteomyelitis: emergency referral. Do not delay for imaging. Bloods (FBC, CRP), blood culture if febrile.
2. Transient synovitis: supportive; review if not improving. NICE NG143, CKS.

tools.title: Measles
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive; notify public health. Vitamin A in areas of deficiency or severe disease.
2. Refer if complications: encephalitis, pneumonia, severe dehydration. MMR for prevention. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Meningitis – viral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Fever + non-blanching rash
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Treat as meningococcal disease until proved otherwise. Immediate parenteral antibiotic (ceftriaxone or benzylpenicillin). Emergency admission. NICE NG51.

options.label: No fever, well child
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider ITP, HSP. FBC, clotting. Refer paediatrics if unwell or platelets <20. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Molluscum – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Self-limiting
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Usually resolve in 6–18 months. Reassurance; avoid squeezing. Consider topical (e.g. potassium hydroxide) or referral if extensive/facial. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Mumps
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive: analgesia, fluids. Notify public health. Avoid contact with non-immune.
2. Refer if meningoencephalitis, orchitis (supportive + consider analgesia), pancreatitis. MMR for prevention. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Murmur – innocent
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Innocent murmur: soft, systolic, varies with position, no other signs. Reassure; no echo needed.
2. Refer if symptomatic, diastolic, harsh, or uncertain. Echo for suspected structural. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Nappy rash
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Barrier cream (e.g. zinc); frequent nappy changes; air time. If candida (satellite lesions): add topical antifungal (e.g. clotrimazole).
2. Refer if severe, infected, or not improving. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Neonate – sepsis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Low Risk (Green)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting and follow-up. Provide written instructions on when to seek help. NICE NG51.

options.label: High Risk (Amber/Red)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
999 Ambulance. NEWS2 score calculation. ABCDE assessment. O2 to target 94-98%. IV access. Pre-hospital antibiotics if >1h from hospital. NICE NG51.

tools.title: Nocturnal enuresis
tools.evidence: Management per NG111 and CKS Bedwetting.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nocturnal: Enuresis alarm first-line; desmopressin if alarm not suitable or for short-term (e.g. sleepover). Reward systems.
2. Daytime wetting: Exclude UTI/constipation; bladder diary; timed voiding. Refer if persistent or red flags. NICE NG111, CKS.

tools.title: Nocturnal enuresis – alarm
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:

1. Nocturnal: Enuresis alarm first-line; desmopressin if alarm not suitable or for short-term (e.g. sleepover). Reward systems.
2. Daytime wetting: Exclude UTI/constipation; bladder diary; timed voiding. Refer if persistent or red flags. NICE NG111, CKS.

tools.title: Osgood-Schlatter
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance: self-limiting; resolves when growth plate fuses. Rest from aggravating activity; ice after sport; simple analgesia.
2. Physiotherapy: quadriceps stretching and strengthening. Consider patellar strap.
3. Refer if diagnostic uncertainty, severe pain, or bilateral with systemic features. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Osteomyelitis – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Soft tissue / tendon
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rest, ice, analgesia; physio. Plantar fasciitis: stretch, orthotics. Tennis elbow: eccentric exercises. Rotator cuff: physio; consider injection. NICE CKS, NG124.

options.label: Joint / arthritis / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GCA: urgent high-dose steroid; refer. Polymyalgia: steroid; monitor. Pseudogout: NSAID. Septic arthritis: emergency referral. NICE NG210, NG100.

tools.title: Otitis media – recurrent
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Mastoiditis (postauricular swelling, protrusion), facial palsy, intracranial complications, recurrent AOM (≥3 in 6 months or ≥4 in 12 months). Consider grommets. NICE NG91.

tools.title: Paediatric dietary allergy – Management
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History: timing, IgE vs non-IgE. Consider SPT/sIgE if IgE-mediated. Trial exclusion for non-IgE.
2. Refer if anaphylaxis, multiple foods, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CG116.

tools.title: Paediatric rash – viral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Most viral rashes: supportive. Exclude meningococcal (non-blanching, unwell), Kawasaki, HSP.
2. Safety-net: Traffic light (NG143). Refer if non-blanching, fever + unwell, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG143, CKS.

tools.title: Perthes disease
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspected Perthes (limp, hip/knee pain, 4–8 years): Urgent orthopaedic referral. X-ray and/or MRI.
2. Avoid weight-bearing if confirmed; physiotherapy; containment if indicated. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Phimosis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Circumcision: Not routinely recommended for physiological phimosis (resolves with time). If pathological phimosis or parental request after discussion: refer to paediatric surgery/urology.
2. Phimosis: Topical steroid (e.g. betamethasone 0.05% once daily for 4–8 weeks) if ballooning or infection; refer if failed or scarring. NICE CKS.
3. Hypospadias: Refer to paediatric urology (surgical correction). Do not circumcise before referral. NICE NG11, NG111, CKS.

tools.title: Pneumonia – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Low Risk (Score 0-1)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG138):
1. Treatment: Amoxicillin 500mg tds for 5 days. 
2. Allergic: Doxycycline 200mg day 1 then 100mg OD, or Clarithromycin 500mg bd.
3. Note: Do not use dual antibiotics for low-risk CAP. NICE NG138.

options.label: Moderate / High Risk (Score ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Consider hospital admission for Score 2; Mandatory for Score ≥ 3.
2. Dual Antibiotics (Moderate): Amoxicillin + Clarithromycin.
3. High Severity: Co-amoxiclav + Clarithromycin (usually IV in hospital). NICE NG138.

tools.title: Postnatal care  the maternal 6-week check – Management
tools.evidence: (Intro removed; no clinical content in this segment.)

options.label: Consultant Care Ethos
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Priority**: Balance the needs of maternal mental health with fetal/infant safety.
2. **Meds**: Avoid 'blind' stopping of effective medication in pregnancy; risk of relapse is high. Consult specialized databases (e.g. BUMPS).
3. **Safety**: Vigilant monitoring for Postpartum Psychosis—a true psychiatric emergency.
4. **Support**: Immediate referral to Specialist Perinatal Mental Health Teams (PMHT).

options.label: Depression / Psychosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Postnatal Depression (PND): SSRIs (Sertraline/Paroxetine) generally preferred if breastfeeding (low milk excretion).
2. Postpartum Psychosis: **Psychiatric Emergency**. Immediate referral to Parent & Baby Unit (MBU). Specialist management with Lithium/Antipsychotics. High risk of infanticide/suicide. NICE CG192.

tools.title: Precocious puberty
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent paediatric endocrinology referral: puberty before 8 (girls) or 9 (boys). LH/FSH, oestradiol/testosterone, bone age, pelvic USS (girls).
2. Treat underlying cause; GnRH analogue if central precocious puberty. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management

tools.title: Thyroid – child
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:

tools.title: Wheeze – viral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Step 1: SABA prn
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Symptoms < 3 times/week and no night-waking.
2. Warning: If using SABA ≥3 times/week, move to Step 2. BTS/SIGN Guidelines.

options.label: Step 2: Low-dose ICS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Beclometasone (e.g. Clenil 100mcg bd). Prevents airway remodelling and reduces exacerbation risk. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Step 3: Add LABA (Combined Inhaler)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: ICS + LABA (e.g. Fostair or Symbicort). MART (Maintenance and Reliever Therapy) is the specialist preference for improved adherence.
2. Review: If still poorly controlled on moderate-dose ICS+LABA, consider LTRA (Montelukast). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Moderate (PEFR 50-75% best)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treatment: SABA 2-5 puffs via spacer every 10-20 mins. Oral Prednisolone 40-50mg for 5 days. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Severe (PEFR 33-50% / RR ≥ 25 / HR ≥ 110)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Immediate hospital admission (999). High-flow Oxygen. Nebulised SABA + Ipratropium. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Life-Threatening (PEFR <33% / SpO2 <92% / Silent Chest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999. Do not delay. Life-threatening features (33-92-CHEST). BTS/SIGN.

tools.title: Autism – Management
tools.evidence: Today we will be discussing autism. With me today I have [Name] who works as a salary GP in County Durham and as a teaching fellow at Newcastle University's Medical School. She's also a mom to two autistic children. Thank you so much for joining me today Nikki.

options.label: Consultant Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Ethos**: Transition from a 'medical model' (fixing deficits) to a 'social model' (adjusting environment).
2. **Co-morbidity**: High rates of ADHD, Anxiety, and Dyspraxia. Always screen for co-occurring conditions.
3. **Biological**: Meds have NO role in core ASD features. Used only for co-morbidities (e.g. Melatonin for sleep, SSRIs for OCD).
4. **Social**: Educational (EHCP) and Workplace adjustments are the primary interventions.

options.label: Child/Young Person
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Local multi-agency ASD pathway (Paediatrics/CAMHS).
2. Screening: SCQ (Social Communication Questionnaire). 
3. Assessment: ADOS and ADI-R (Gold standard tools).

options.label: Adult suspected ASD

tools.title: CKD – hypertension
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

options.label: Non-visible (≥45 or risk factors)
options.guidance:

options.label: Man
options.guidance:

options.label: Pregnant Woman
options.guidance:

options.label: Child / recurrent / pyelonephritis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

2. Recurrent: Consider prophylaxis (nitrofurantoin at night) or self-start. Pyelonephritis: Send MSU, consider admission or 7–14 days oral (e.g. cefalexin). NICE NG109.

tools.title: Managing male LUTS  causes, assessment and treatment in primary care – Management
tools.evidence: Now in this episode I want to discuss lower urinary tract symptoms or luts in men as this has not only been requested as a topic by a listener to the podcast so many thanks for getting in touch about this but which also represents a highly prevalent and clinically significant pre…

options.label: LUTS: Medical 1st-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Alpha-blocker: Tamsulosin 400mcg OD (for rapid flow relief).
2. 5-ARI: Finasteride 5mg OD (if prostate > 30g). Warn: takes 6 months for effect and reduces PSA by 50%.
3. Anticholinergic: Add e.g. Solifenacin if storage symptoms (urgency) persist despite alpha-blocker. BAUS.

options.label: Surgical Triggers (Consultant Referral)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Recurrent urinary retention, bladder stones, haematuria (prostate origin), or renal impairment due to obstruction.
2. Note: Refer for consideration of TURP, Greenlight Laser, or UroLift. BAUS.

options.label: Suspected Torsion (Emergency)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BAUS):
1. Presentation: Sudden onset pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex.
2. Action: Immediate Urology referral for exploration (window < 6h). Do not wait for ultrasound if clinical torsion suspected.

options.label: Epididymo-orchitis (Infection)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treatment: Ceftriaxone 1g IM + Doxycycline 100mg bd for 14 days (if STI risk) OR Ofloxacin 200mg bd for 14 days (UTI association).
2. Note: Always use STI-base cover in men < 35y.

tools.title: Membranous nephropathy
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Usually presents with nephrotic syndrome (oedema, hypoalbuminaemia, proteinuria). Confirm diagnosis (renal biopsy); exclude secondary causes (malignancy, HBV/HCV, SLE, drugs).
2. Refer nephrology: immunosuppression (e.g. rituximab, cyclophosphamide/steroid) per KDIGO/NICE. ACEi/ARB for proteinuria; treat hypertension; thromboprophylaxis if nephrotic. NICE NG203, CKS.

2. Supportive: fluid/salt restriction; diuretics; thromboprophylaxis if severe. Treat infection. NICE NG203, CKS.

tools.title: Renal colic
tools.evidence: Management per CKS Renal colic.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pain: NSAIDs first-line (any route); paracetamol if contraindicated; opioids only if both insufficient. Do not offer antispasmodics.
2. Imaging: Low-dose non-contrast CT within 24h (adults); USS in pregnancy/children; consider CT if diagnosis uncertain in children.
3. Alpha-blocker may be considered for distal ureteric stone <10mm (medical expulsive therapy).
4. Urgent/emergency referral: sepsis, obstructed infected kidney, uncontrolled pain, AKI/anuria, diagnostic uncertainty (e.g. AAA, peritonitis). Routine follow-up in primary care if pain controlled. NICE NG118, CKS Renal colic.

tools.title: Contraception – breastfeeding
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Combined Hormonal (CHC) - UKMEC
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Screening: BP, BMI, Migraine with aura (MEC 4), Smoking >35y (MEC 4), VTE history (MEC 4).
2. Missed Pill: 24h+ late? Check FSRH missed pill tool. Usually, 1 pill missed = take ASAP and no extra care. 2+ pills = extra care for 7 days.
3. Breakout Bleeding: Exclude STI. If persist, increase oestrogen dose or change progestogen type.

options.label: Long-Acting (LARC)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Mirena/Levosert: Now licensed for 8 years for contraception (if fitted age ≥25).
2. Nexplanon: Effective for 3 years. Inform about irregular bleeding pattern.
3. Copper IUD: Non-hormonal. Gold standard for emergency contraception (within 5 days).

options.label: Emergency Contraception
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Copper IUD: Most effective (MEC 1 in majority). Up to 5 days after UPSI.
2. Ulipristal (ellaOne): Up to 5 days (120h). Avoid progestogens for 5 days after ellaOne.
3. Levonorgestrel: Up to 3 days (72h). Double dose (3mg) if BMI >30 or on enzyme-inducers.

tools.title: Contraception – migraine
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: First-line: Stratified Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH Guidelines):
1. Combined Approach: Soluble Aspirin (900mg) or Naproxen (500mg) + Triptan (e.g. Sumatriptan 50-100mg) + Prokinetic Anti-emetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
2. Note: Treat early at onset of headache, not aura. Avoid opioids (risk of Medication Overuse Headache). NICE NG150.

options.label: Triptan Failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Switch: Trial different triptan or different formulation (e.g. Sumatriptan Nasal Spray or SC).
2. MOH: Review for Medication Overuse Headache if using triptans ≥ 10 days/month. NICE NG150.

options.label: Initial Choice (Indicated if ≥2 attacks/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH/RCP):
1. First-line choices: Propranolol (80-160mg), Amitriptyline (10-50mg nocte), or Topiramate (titrate to 50mg-100mg - warn about teratogenicity/birth control).
2. Second-line: Candesartan (8-16mg) - widely used by neurologists off-label but supported by evidence. NICE NG150.

options.label: Specialist Interventions (Consultant Care)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CGRP Monoclonals (e.g. Erenumab, Fremanezumab): Indicated if ≥4 migraine days/month and failure of 3 oral preventatives. NICE TA.
2. Botox: Protocolized 31-site injection (PREEMPT) if chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, 8 being migraine). NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: Red flags / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: Thunderclap (SAH), new sudden severe, fever + neck stiffness (meningitis), papilloedema.
2. Refer: New headache ≥50y, progressive, positional, or focal neurology. NICE NG150, NG51.

tools.title: Contraception – perimenopause
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Diagnosis (BMS Toolkit)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Clinical: >45y with vasomotor symptoms and irregular periods (perimenopause) or no period ≥1y (menopause).
2. FSH: Only if <40 (premature) or 40-45 with atypia. Do not use FSH if on hormonal contraception.
3. Discussion: Review benefits vs risks (low risk in <60y/within 10y of onset). NICE NG23 / BMS.

options.label: HRT: Systemic Treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BMS Gold Standard):
1. Choice: Transdermal (Gel/Patch) preferred if BMI >30, Migraine, or high VTE risk.
2. Progesterone: Micronised Progesterone (Utrogestan) 100mg nocte (continuous) or 200mg (cyclical days 15-26) is the metabolic gold standard.
3. Mirena IUS: Excellent for endometrial protection and contraception.
4. Testosterone: Trial if low libido despite adequate oestrogen (specialist initiation). BMS.

options.label: Atrophic Vaginitis (GSM)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topicals: Vaginal Oestriol (Ovestin) or Estradiol (Vagifem/Imvaggis). Use daily for 2w then twice weekly indefinitely.
2. Note: Safe to use long-term even if systemic HRT contraindicated (discuss with oncology if breast cancer). NICE NG23.

tools.title: Contraception – VTE
tools.evidence: NICE NG158: Wells score for DVT/PE; D-dimer (age-adjusted if >50). Imaging within 4h if likely DVT; CTPA for PE. DOAC 3 months minimum; extend if unprovoked or high risk.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):
1. Action: Urgent Proximal Leg US within 4h (or interim anticoagulation if wait >4h).
2. Result: If US negative but D-dimer positive, repeat US in 6-8 days.

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Immediate: CTPA (Computed Tomographic Pulmonary Angiography). Interim anticoagulation (e.g. Apixaban 10mg bd) if scan delayed >1h.
2. V/Q Scan: Preferred if renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe allergy to contrast.
3. Note: If PE likely, assess PESI score for suitability of outpatient management.

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).
2. Refer: Anticoagulation failure, thrombophilia testing (young, family history), cancer-associated. NICE NG158.

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 months (provoked/low risk), 6 months+ or indefinite (unprovoked or recurrence). NICE NG158.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

tools.title: Ectopic pregnancy
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

tools.title: Effective contraception provision during the COVID-19 pandemic – Management
tools.evidence: Now the Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare, FSRH has produced some useful and pragmatic recommendations to help us in primary care support women of all ages with contraceptive requirements during this COVID-19 pandemic as we cut back on non-essential face-to-face conta…

options.label: Combined Hormonal (CHC) - UKMEC
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Screening: BP, BMI, Migraine with aura (MEC 4), Smoking >35y (MEC 4), VTE history (MEC 4).
2. Missed Pill: 24h+ late? Check FSRH missed pill tool. Usually, 1 pill missed = take ASAP and no extra care. 2+ pills = extra care for 7 days.
3. Breakout Bleeding: Exclude STI. If persist, increase oestrogen dose or change progestogen type.

options.label: Long-Acting (LARC)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Mirena/Levosert: Now licensed for 8 years for contraception (if fitted age ≥25).
2. Nexplanon: Effective for 3 years. Inform about irregular bleeding pattern.
3. Copper IUD: Non-hormonal. Gold standard for emergency contraception (within 5 days).

options.label: Emergency Contraception
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Copper IUD: Most effective (MEC 1 in majority). Up to 5 days after UPSI.
2. Ulipristal (ellaOne): Up to 5 days (120h). Avoid progestogens for 5 days after ellaOne.
3. Levonorgestrel: Up to 3 days (72h). Double dose (3mg) if BMI >30 or on enzyme-inducers.

tools.title: Endometrial cancer – 2WW
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Contraception / bleeding
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. HMB: Levonorgestrel IUS, tranexamic acid. IMB/PCB: speculum; swabs; 2WW if PMB. Contraception: choice per need; POP/COCP/implant/IUD per CKS.
2. NICE NG88, NG3, CKS.

options.label: Infection / pain / 2WW
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Vaginal infection: Candida/BV/Trichomonas – treat per CKS. Pelvic pain: exclude PID; consider endometriosis. 2WW: breast lump, PMB, cervical/ovarian/endometrial concern. NICE NG12, NG3.

options.label: Vaginal discharge – when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Candida: topical clotrimazole or oral fluconazole. BV: metronidazole. Trichomonas: metronidazole; treat contacts. 2WW: postmenopausal bleeding, cervical concern. Refer if recurrent, pregnant, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CKS, NG12.

tools.title: Endometriosis
tools.evidence: Management per NG73 and CKS Endometriosis.

options.label: Heavy Menstrual Bleeding (HMB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG88):
1. 1st-line: Mirena IUS (if acceptable).
2. 2nd-line: Tranexamic Acid (1g tds during period) +/- Mefenamic Acid (500mg tds).
3. Hormonal: COCP or High-dose Progestogens (Medroxyprogesterone).
4. Investigation: Pelvic US if uterus large/fibroids, or fail medical tx.

options.label: PCOS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BMS/RCOG):
1. Diagnosis: Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: Anovulation, Hyperandrogenism, Polycystic ovaries).
2. Protection: Prevent endometrial hyperplasia via IUS or COCP (ensure ≥4 bleeds/year).
3. Metabolic: Screen for T2DM (HbA1c) and CVD risk. Metformin if insulin resistant. NICE NG28, CKS PCOS.

options.label: Endometriosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG73):
1. Trial: 3-6 months COCP or POP. NSAIDs for pain.
2. Imaging: Pelvic US (specialist endometriosis scan if deep involvement suspected).
3. Referral: To BSGE Endometriosis centre if severe/refractory or bowel/bladder involvement.

options.label: Post-Menopausal Bleeding (PMB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG/NICE):
1. Triage: Any vaginal bleeding in a post-menopausal woman not on HRT, or unexpected bleeding on HRT.
2. Action: Urgent 2WW Referral for Ultrasound +/- Hysteroscopy/Biopsy.
3. Cut-off: Endometrial thickness > 4mm in PMB requires biopsy. NICE NG12.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Cold sore
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aciclovir 5% cream 5×/day 5 days, or oral aciclovir 200 mg 5×/day 5 days if early/severe.
2. Suppression: consider if ≥6 episodes/year. NICE CKS.

options.label: First episode genital
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aciclovir 400 mg tds 7–10 days (or valaciclovir). Screen for other STIs. Counsel on transmission.
2. Suppression if recurrent. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Gestational diabetes – follow-up
tools.evidence: NICE NG28: HbA1c targets by context (48–53 mmol/mol). SGLT2i for CVD/HF/CKD; GLP-1 for obesity where indicated. Annual review: foot check, kidney, cardiovascular risk.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

options.label: No uterus – oestrogen only
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oestrogen only (patch/gel preferred for VTE risk). Review annually. NICE NG23.

options.label: With uterus – combined
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oestrogen + cyclical or continuous progestogen. Sequential if perimenopausal; continuous if postmenopausal. NICE NG23.

options.label: Contraindications / alternatives
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Contraindications: breast cancer, VTE, stroke. Consider non-hormonal (clonidine, CBT) or topical oestrogen for urogenital. NICE NG23.

options.label: Benign Lumps (Indications for GP Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Symptomatic (pain, inflammation, interference with function). 
2. Lipomas: Usually only if >5cm or rapidly growing (refer for US first to exclude sarcoma).
3. Sebaceous Cysts: Excise if recurrently infected (wait for infection to settle first).
4. Exclusions: Cosmetic removal is generally not NHS-funded.

options.label: Red Flags (Refer to 2WW / Plastic Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Changing Naevi: Refer to 2WW Dermatology.
2. Irregular, fixed, or hard masses: Urgent referral.
3. Note: Never excise a lesion where malignancy is suspected in primary care minor surgery clinic.

tools.title: Postnatal – depression
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Holistic Consultant Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Biological**: Antidepressants (SSRIs 1st-line) + optimize physical health (sleep/exercise/thyroid).
2. **Psychological**: Evidence-based CBT, IPT, or Psychodynamic therapy. Strategy is to change cognitive distorting loops.
3. **Social**: Stabilize housing, employment, and social isolation. Review significant relational stressors.
4. **Remission Goal**: Total symptomatic relief, not just improvement. Continue meds for 6-12 months post-recovery. NICE NG222.

options.label: MDD Diagnosis (DSM-5 / PHQ-9)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Core: ≥5 of 9 symptoms for ≥2 weeks. Must include Mood or Anhedonia.
2. Severity Stratification: 
   - Mild: PHQ-9 10-14. 
   - Moderate: PHQ-9 15-19.
   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

tools.title: Pregnancy – booking
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

tools.title: Pregnancy – diabetes
tools.evidence: NICE NG28: HbA1c targets by context (48–53 mmol/mol). SGLT2i for CVD/HF/CKD; GLP-1 for obesity where indicated. Annual review: foot check, kidney, cardiovascular risk.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

tools.title: Pregnancy – epilepsy
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: First Seizure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Urgency: Refer to 'First Seizure Clinic' (within 2 weeks). NICE NG217.
2. Investigation: EEG + MRI Brain (Standard protocol including coronal T2/FLAIR sessions). 
3. Safety: High-risk activities (driving, swimming, working at heights) must stop until specialist review.

options.label: Focal Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Lamotrigine or Levetiracetam (Keppra). NICE NG217.

options.label: Generalized Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Sodium Valproate (Epilim) - **Strict warning: Not for use in women/girls of childbearing potential unless Pregnancy Prevention Programme in place.**
2. Alternative: Levetiracetam or Lamotrigine.

tools.title: Pregnancy – hypertension
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

tools.title: Pregnancy – nausea
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Symptomatic relief
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify cause (GI, drugs, vestibular, metabolic, CNS). Cyclizine 50 mg tds or prochlorperazine 5 mg tds; metoclopramide 10 mg tds (avoid if young or parkinsonism).
2. Red flags: Headache, abdominal pain, dehydration – assess and refer as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit: Severe dehydration, suspected bowel obstruction, head injury, raised ICP. 2WW: Unexplained persistent nausea/vomiting with weight loss.
2. Pregnancy: Exclude hyperemesis; treat and refer if severe. NICE NG12, CKS.

tools.title: Pregnancy – thyroid
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Small / fluctuant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

options.label: Recurrent boils
options.guidance:

1. Hygiene; nasal decolonisation (mupirocin) if nasal carriage. Screen household. Consider referral if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Listen; address concerns with evidence. Offer reliable resources (NHS, PHE). No coercion.

tools.title: Bite – animal
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: HIV / TB / viral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. HIV: test; PrEP/PEP per NICE. TB: refer TB service; RIPE. COVID antiviral: per eligibility. Shingles: aciclovir if <72 h; 2WW if ophthalmic. NICE NG33, NG122, CKS.

options.label: Bites / travel / other
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bite: clean; antibiotic if high risk; rabies/tetanus. Needlestick: risk assess; PEP if source high risk. Travel: advise vaccines; malaria prophylaxis. NICE CKS.

options.label: Tick bite / Lyme
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Remove tick with fine-tipped tweezers. Prophylaxis: doxycycline 200 mg single dose if attached ≥36 h and endemic area. Erythema migrans: doxycycline 100 mg bd 21 days. Refer if neurological/joint. NICE NG95, CKS.

options.label: Needlestick / sharps
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Wash; encourage bleeding. Risk assess: source HIV/HBV/HCV status. HBV: check immunity; offer vaccine/immunoglobulin. HIV: PEP within 72 h per local protocol. Baseline bloods; follow-up. NICE NG33, CKS.

options.label: Mild / moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

2. Mark margin; review at 48 h. NICE NG141.

options.label: Severe / facial / systemic
options.guidance:

tools.title: Conjunctivitis
tools.evidence: Management per CKS Conjunctivitis.

options.label: Bacterial Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Chloramphenicol 0.5% drops 2-hourly for 2 days then qds. Fusidic acid if pregnant. Safety-net for pain/vision loss. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected Corneal Ulcer/Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Contact lens wearer? Painful? Fluorescein staining positive? Emergency Ophthalmology referral (same day). Avoid steroids.

options.label: Scleritis (Deep pain)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Deep, boring eye pain. Systemic associations (rheumatoid). Urgent Ophthalmology referral (within 24-48h). NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / red eye warning
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: Pain, photophobia, reduced vision, contact lens wear, trauma, chemical injury.
2. Urgent: Viral keratitis (dendritic), scleritis, acute glaucoma. Avoid steroids until cause known. NICE CKS.

MANAGEMENT PLAN:

options.label: Severe / facial / systemic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

options.label: Periorbital / orbital / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Periorbital: Swelling limited to lids; oral antibiotics; same-day review if worsening.

options.label: Joint / arthritis / red flags

tools.title: Scabies – crusted
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Standard
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

options.label: Crusted
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer dermatology. Ivermectin (unlicensed) or permethrin under supervision. CKS Scabies.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Permethrin preferred; avoid ivermectin (limited data). Treat contacts. 2. Refer: Crusted, institutional outbreak, or treatment failure. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Varicella – pregnancy
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Management: Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for distress (not for fever alone).
2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

options.label: Amber (Intermediate Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assessment: Check for focus (ears, urine, chest). Consider urine dip.
2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.label: Red (High Risk / Sepsis)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

tools.title: Vitamin B12 supplementation during the COVID-19 pandemic – Management
tools.evidence: Now the British Society for Himatology, BSH, updated their guidance on Vitamin B12 replacement during this Covid-19 pandemic on Friday 24th April. And overall this iteration of the guidance appears less prescriptive on omitting Vitamin B12 injections and also emphasises the impor…

options.label: B12 Deficiency - Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-dietary (e.g. Pernicious Anaemia): Hydroxocobalamin 1mg IM every other day for 2 weeks (loading), then 1mg IM every 3 months for life.
2. Dietary: Oral cyanocobalamin 50-150mcg daily between meals, or two 1mg injections per year.
3. Monitoring: Reticulocyte count at 7-10 days; Hb/MCV at 8 weeks.
4. Review: Exclude co-existing Iron/Folate deficiency if response sub-optimal. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Zika
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: HIV / TB / viral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. HIV: test; PrEP/PEP per NICE. TB: refer TB service; RIPE. COVID antiviral: per eligibility. Shingles: aciclovir if <72 h; 2WW if ophthalmic. NICE NG33, NG122, CKS.

options.label: Bites / travel / other
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bite: clean; antibiotic if high risk; rabies/tetanus. Needlestick: risk assess; PEP if source high risk. Travel: advise vaccines; malaria prophylaxis. NICE CKS.

options.label: Tick bite / Lyme
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Remove tick with fine-tipped tweezers. Prophylaxis: doxycycline 200 mg single dose if attached ≥36 h and endemic area. Erythema migrans: doxycycline 100 mg bd 21 days. Refer if neurological/joint. NICE NG95, CKS.

options.label: Needlestick / sharps
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Wash; encourage bleeding. Risk assess: source HIV/HBV/HCV status. HBV: check immunity; offer vaccine/immunoglobulin. HIV: PEP within 72 h per local protocol. Baseline bloods; follow-up. NICE NG33, CKS.

tools.title: Carpal tunnel – referral
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild to Moderate (Sensory only / Nocturnal symptoms)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Specialist Care):
1. Primary: Targeted corticosteroid injection (e.g. 20-40mg Methylprednisolone) into carpal tunnel. Highly effective for symptom relief.
2. Splintage: Mandatory neutral-angle nocturnal wrist splints for 8 weeks.
3. Neuro-monitoring: Repeat NCS in 3-6 months if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Severe (Motor deficit / Thenar atrophy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Surgical Care):
1. Gold Standard: Open or endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release (CTR).
2. Urgency: Required within 4-8 weeks to prevent irreversible axotomy/atrophy.
3. NCS Findings: Expect prolonged distal motor latency (DML > 4.5ms) and absent/reduced amplitudes.

tools.title: Cauda equina syndrome – Management
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Emergency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Saddle numbness, retention, bilateral leg weakness – emergency MRI and neurosurgery. Do not delay. NICE NG59.

tools.title: Cervicogenic headache
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: First-line: Stratified Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH Guidelines):
1. Combined Approach: Soluble Aspirin (900mg) or Naproxen (500mg) + Triptan (e.g. Sumatriptan 50-100mg) + Prokinetic Anti-emetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
2. Note: Treat early at onset of headache, not aura. Avoid opioids (risk of Medication Overuse Headache). NICE NG150.

options.label: Triptan Failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Switch: Trial different triptan or different formulation (e.g. Sumatriptan Nasal Spray or SC).
2. MOH: Review for Medication Overuse Headache if using triptans ≥ 10 days/month. NICE NG150.

options.label: Initial Choice (Indicated if ≥2 attacks/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH/RCP):
1. First-line choices: Propranolol (80-160mg), Amitriptyline (10-50mg nocte), or Topiramate (titrate to 50mg-100mg - warn about teratogenicity/birth control).
2. Second-line: Candesartan (8-16mg) - widely used by neurologists off-label but supported by evidence. NICE NG150.

options.label: Specialist Interventions (Consultant Care)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CGRP Monoclonals (e.g. Erenumab, Fremanezumab): Indicated if ≥4 migraine days/month and failure of 3 oral preventatives. NICE TA.
2. Botox: Protocolized 31-site injection (PREEMPT) if chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, 8 being migraine). NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: Red flags / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: Thunderclap (SAH), new sudden severe, fever + neck stiffness (meningitis), papilloedema.
2. Refer: New headache ≥50y, progressive, positional, or focal neurology. NICE NG150, NG51.

tools.title: Dementia – driving
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Philosophy of Dementia Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Approach**: Person-centered care focusing on preserving dignity and functional independence.
2. **Biological**: Managing reversible factors (infection/nutrition) and carefully titrating specialized cognitive enhancers.
3. **Psychological**: Validation therapy and addressing 'met and unmet needs' underlying behavioral symptoms (BPSD).
4. **Social**: Essential focus on Carer Support (respite, benefits) and home safety assessments (Occupational Therapy).

options.label: Alzheimer's Disease (Commonest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Early episodic memory loss, word-finding difficulty.
2. Imaging: Medial temporal lobe atrophy.
3. Meds: AChE inhibitors (Donepezil) or NMDA antagonists (Memantine).

options.label: Vascular Dementia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Stepwise decline, focal neurological signs, executive dysfunction.
2. Management: Aggressive V-risk factor control (BP, Lipids, Diabetes, Antiplatelets).

options.label: Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triad: Visual hallucinations, Parkinsonism, Fluctuating cognition.
2. **CRITICAL WARNING**: Extreme sensitivity to antipsychotics (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome risk). Use Quetiapine or Clozapine with extreme caution if BPSD severe.

options.label: Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Personality change, disinhibition, hyperoriality, or language decline (Primary Progressive Aphasia).
2. Management: SSRIs (e.g. Paroxetine) for behavioral symptoms. AChE inhibitors may worsen agitation in FTD.

options.label: Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Step 1: Rule out delirium (UTI/Pain/Meds/Constipation/Dehydration).
2. Step 2: Non-pharmacological (Life story work, music therapy).
3. Step 3: Pharmacological (Risperidone 0.25-0.5mg max 6w). Consider Trazodone or Lorazepam for acute severe distress. NICE NG97.

tools.title: Diagnosis and management of vertigo in primary care – Management
tools.evidence: Welcome to our new season of [Organisation] Podcasts. Bite Size regular charts for all of us working in primary care. Class will cover clinical tips and hacks as well as hot topics to help make our lives a wee bit easier but ultimately to help improve the lives of our patients in…

options.label: BPPV (Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Dix-Hallpike maneuver (torsional nystagmus).
2. Treatment: Epley maneuver (specialist physio or trained clinician). NICE CKS.

options.label: Vestibular Migraine / Meniere's
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Meniere's: Triad of Vertigo, Hearing loss, and Tinnitus. Treatment: Prochlorperazine (acute) + Betahistine (prophylaxis).
2. Vertigo Red Flags: Central vertigo (negative HINTS exam), new focal neurology → Urgent MRI/A&E.

tools.title: Epilepsy – driving
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: First Seizure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Urgency: Refer to 'First Seizure Clinic' (within 2 weeks). NICE NG217.
2. Investigation: EEG + MRI Brain (Standard protocol including coronal T2/FLAIR sessions). 
3. Safety: High-risk activities (driving, swimming, working at heights) must stop until specialist review.

options.label: Focal Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Lamotrigine or Levetiracetam (Keppra). NICE NG217.

options.label: Generalized Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Sodium Valproate (Epilim) - **Strict warning: Not for use in women/girls of childbearing potential unless Pregnancy Prevention Programme in place.**
2. Alternative: Levetiracetam or Lamotrigine.

tools.title: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

tools.title: Parkinson's – psychosis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Philosophy of Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Safety First**: Immediate risk assessment for Bipolar/Psychosis. Intent to self-harm or harm others (delusional pull).
2. **Biological Core**: Mood stabilizers (Lithium) and Antipsychotics are non-negotiable for stability. High emphasis on medication adherence.
3. **Social/Rehab**: Early Intervention Services (EIP) focus on maintaining social roles (work/education) during the 'critical period' of the first 3 years.
4. **Long-term**: Prophylaxis to prevent 'kindling' (where each subsequent episode is easier to trigger and harder to treat). NICE CG185, CG178.

options.label: Acute Mania / Hypomania
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE CG185):
1. Stop: Antidepressants immediately.
2. 1st-line: Antipsychotic (Haloperidol, Olanzapine, Quetiapine, or Risperidone).
3. Failure: Trial 2nd antipsychotic. Lithium as 3rd-line in acute phase.
4. Type distinction: Bipolar I (Full mania, often requires admission); Bipolar II (Hypomania + Severe Depression).

options.label: Bipolar Depression
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choices: Quetiapine (monotherapy), Olanzapine + Fluoxetine, or Lamotrigine (titrate slowly to prevent SJS).
2. Avoid: Antidepressant monotherapy (risk of switch to mania). NICE CG185.

options.label: Maintenance (Lithium)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target Level: 0.6-1.0 mmol/L.
2. Monitoring: Levels q3m (initially q1w). TFT/U&E/Calcium q6m.
3. Toxicity: Coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, confusion. Emergency A&E. NICE CG185.

options.label: Early Intervention (EIP)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Mandatory within 24h of suspected First Episode Psychosis (FEP).
2. Pharmacology: Oral atypical antipsychotic (Aripiprazole or Risperidone low-dose). NICE CG178.

options.label: Treatment Resistant Schizophrenia (TRS)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of 2x antipsychotics (at least one 2nd-gen) for ≥6 weeks at optimal dose.
2. Clozapine: **The only evidence-based treatment for TRS**. Mandatory FBC monitoring (risk of agranulocytosis). Specialist initiation only. NICE CG178.

options.label: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Emergency (ENT same day). High-dose oral Prednisolone (e.g. 60mg OD for 7 days) started immediately. Urgent Audiogram. NICE NG98.

options.label: Unilateral Pulsatile Tinnitus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Urgent ENT referral for imaging (exclude glomus tumour/vascular malformation). Routine referral if non-pulsatile but persistent/distressing. NICE NG155.

options.label: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Valsalva manoeuvre. Nasal steroid spray (e.g. Fluticasone) for 4-6 weeks if obstructive. Decongestants (short-term only). NICE CKS.

tools.title: Transient loss of consciousness – Management
tools.evidence: You can find Sonor Major podcast platforms including Spotify, Apple podcasts and Google podcasts. Today...

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

tools.title: B12 deficiency
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: B12 Deficiency - Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-dietary (e.g. Pernicious Anaemia): Hydroxocobalamin 1mg IM every other day for 2 weeks (loading), then 1mg IM every 3 months for life.
2. Dietary: Oral cyanocobalamin 50-150mcg daily between meals, or two 1mg injections per year.
3. Monitoring: Reticulocyte count at 7-10 days; Hb/MCV at 8 weeks.
4. Review: Exclude co-existing Iron/Folate deficiency if response sub-optimal. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Recurrent VTE
tools.evidence: NICE NG158: Wells score for DVT/PE; D-dimer (age-adjusted if >50). Imaging within 4h if likely DVT; CTPA for PE. DOAC 3 months minimum; extend if unprovoked or high risk.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):
1. Action: Urgent Proximal Leg US within 4h (or interim anticoagulation if wait >4h).
2. Result: If US negative but D-dimer positive, repeat US in 6-8 days.

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Immediate: CTPA (Computed Tomographic Pulmonary Angiography). Interim anticoagulation (e.g. Apixaban 10mg bd) if scan delayed >1h.
2. V/Q Scan: Preferred if renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe allergy to contrast.
3. Note: If PE likely, assess PESI score for suitability of outpatient management.

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).
2. Refer: Anticoagulation failure, thrombophilia testing (young, family history), cancer-associated. NICE NG158.

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 months (provoked/low risk), 6 months+ or indefinite (unprovoked or recurrence). NICE NG158.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

tools.title: Sideroblastic anaemia
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Iron deficiency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD or bd (or ferrous fumarate). Recheck Hb in 2–4 weeks. Continue 3 months after normal. If not responding: check compliance, consider malabsorption, 2WW if red flags. NICE NG24.

options.label: B12 deficiency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Hydroxocobalamin 1 mg IM 3× per week 2 weeks then 1 mg every 3 months (or oral if mild and compliant). Check folate. NICE NG241.

options.label: Macrocytic (B12/folate)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check B12 and folate. Treat as above. If both normal consider alcohol, hypothyroid, MDS – consider referral. NICE NG24.

options.label: Anaemia of chronic disease / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACD: Normocytic; ferritin often normal or raised; treat underlying condition. IV iron only if functional deficit and CKD or inflammatory barrier.
2. 2WW: Unexplained anaemia, red flags (weight loss, bleeding). NICE NG24, NG12.

tools.title: Acute otitis media
tools.evidence: Management per NG91 and CKS Otitis media.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Mastoiditis (postauricular swelling, protrusion), facial palsy, intracranial complications, recurrent AOM (≥3 in 6 months or ≥4 in 12 months). Consider grommets. NICE NG91.
