tools.title: Alcohol and health  a review of the latest research – Management
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Holistic Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Stages of Change**: Identify where the patient is (Pre-contemplation to Maintenance).
2. **Harm Reduction**: Reducing units, switching to lower ABV, safe drinking intervals. 
3. **Biological**: Supervised detox if dependent (≥10 units/day or morning shakes) followed by anti-craving meds.
4. **Psychosocial**: Engagement with community services (AA, SMART Recovery) and addressing 'dual diagnosis' (co-morbid anxiety/depression).

options.label: Withdrawal Severity & Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Severity: 
   - Mild (CIWA <10): Supportive, vitamins only.
   - Mod/Severe (CIWA ≥10): Chlordiazepoxide regime.
2. **Wernicke's Triad**: Ophthalmoplegia, Ataxia, Confusion. 
3. **CRITICAL**: Give Pabrinex (Thiamine) BEFORE Glucose to prevent precipitating Wernicke's. NICE CG115.

options.label: Anti-Craving Pharmacotherapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Acamprosate**: 666mg tds. Start day 1 of abstinence.
2. **Naltrexone**: 50mg OD. Monitor LFTs.
3. **Disulfiram**: Specialist only. NICE CG115.

tools.title: Allergic rhinitis
tools.evidence: Management per NG79 and CKS Allergic rhinitis.

options.label: Allergic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Intranasal corticosteroid (e.g. beclometasone) first-line; add antihistamine if needed. Avoid sedating antihistamines long-term.
2. Consider allergen avoidance. Refer if severe or not controlled. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / severe
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer ENT/dermatology: Nasal polyps, persistent unilateral symptoms, diagnostic uncertainty. Consider immunotherapy (specialist) if severe and allergen identified.
2. Rule out CSF leak if unilateral watery discharge. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Cows' Milk Protein Allergy  The diagnostic challenge for GPs – Management
tools.evidence: So hello, so I'm [Name]. K Talon. I'm a former pediatric trainee who's changed career path to general practice. And I'm [Name] a GP registrar in the Jessfield scheme. Having come from the pediatric to general practice, I've developed a whole new appreciation for the challenges GP…

options.label: Diagnosis & exclusion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breastfed: Maternal exclusion of cow's milk (and egg if suspected).
2. Formula-fed: Trial extensively hydrolysed formula (EHF) for 2–4 weeks. If IgE-mediated, consider skin prick/sIgE.
3. Reintroduction: Supervised challenge to confirm. NICE CG116, BSACI.

options.label: First-line formula
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-IgE / delayed: EHF (e.g. Nutramigen, Aptamil Pepti).
2. IgE-mediated / anaphylaxis: EHF or amino-acid formula (AAF e.g. Neocate) if EHF not tolerated.
3. Avoid: Soya under 6 months; rice formula not first-line. NICE CG116.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dietitian: If multiple exclusions, faltering growth, or weaning advice.
2. Paediatric allergy: Anaphylaxis, diagnostic uncertainty, or need for AAF. NICE CG116.

tools.title: Epistaxis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: First Aid (Acute)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Position: Lean forward, do not swallow blood.
2. Compression: Firmly pinch lower soft part of nose for 10-15 mins without release.
3. Warnings: If bleeding >15 mins or severe, attend A&E. NICE CKS.

options.label: Primary Care Cautery
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identification: Identify bleeding point (usually Little's area on septum).
2. Technique: Anesthetize then apply Silver Nitrate (75%) for 1-5 seconds.
3. Post-care: Apply Naseptin (check peanut/soy allergy) or petroleum jelly bd for 10 days. NICE CKS.

options.label: Recurrent / Prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Ointment: Apply antiseptic cream (Naseptin) to nostrils bd for 10 days to reduce crusting/infection.
2. Habits: Avoid nose-picking, hot baths, and heavy lifting for 24h after a bleed.
3. Review meds: Review use of anticoagulants/antiplatelets if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / anticoagulation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer ENT: Persistent bleeding despite first aid, posterior bleed, or packing. A&E if haemodynamically unstable.
2. Anticoagulation: Do not stop DOAC/warfarin routinely; treat locally. Consider temporary hold only if severe recurrent and discussed with haematology. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Eustachian tube dysfunction
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Emergency (ENT same day). High-dose oral Prednisolone (e.g. 60mg OD for 7 days) started immediately. Urgent Audiogram. NICE NG98.

options.label: Unilateral Pulsatile Tinnitus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Urgent ENT referral for imaging (exclude glomus tumour/vascular malformation). Routine referral if non-pulsatile but persistent/distressing. NICE NG155.

options.label: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Valsalva manoeuvre. Nasal steroid spray (e.g. Fluticasone) for 4-6 weeks if obstructive. Decongestants (short-term only). NICE CKS.

tools.title: Fungal sinusitis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Likely viral (<10 days)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Advise if no improvement by 10 days or worsening, re-assess. NICE NG79.

options.label: Persistent or severe
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider phenoxymethylpenicillin or co-amoxiclav 7 days if no improvement after 10 days or severe. NICE NG79.

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Orbital/cranial complications, frontal swelling, severe headache, double vision, reduced consciousness.
2. Consider 2WW if chronic sinusitis or recurrent. NICE NG79, NG12.

options.label: Allergic
options.guidance:

tools.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea – ENT
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Suspected OSA (NICE NG202)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Score: Use **Epworth Sleepiness Scale** (>10 is abnormal).
2. Risk: Assess for comorbidities (BMI >30, HTN, Diabetes).
3. Referral: Sleep clinic for Nocturnal Oximetry or Polysomnography.
4. Driving: Advise patient to inform DVLA if excessive daytime sleepiness affects driving. NICE NG202.

tools.title: Osteoporosis  key learnings from the NOGG 2024 clinical guideline – Management
tools.evidence: Join us for a whole range of bite-sized topics tailored for those working in primary care. Perfect for your daily commute or when you're out on a morning stroll. You can tune into us on all leading podcast platforms and don't forget to like and subscribe so you don't miss an epis…

options.label: Osteoporosis – fracture / DEXA
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. FRAX; DEXA if indicated. Calcium + vitamin D. First-line: oral bisphosphonate (alendronate/risedronate); ensure correct administration. Consider IV zoledronate if oral not tolerated. NICE NG146, CKS.

options.label: Osteoporosis – denosumab / teriparatide
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Denosumab: 6-monthly SC; do not miss doses (rebound fracture risk). Monitor calcium/vitamin D. Teriparatide: specialist; limited duration. NICE NG146, CKS.

options.label: Osteomalacia / Paget's
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Osteomalacia: vitamin D repletion; treat cause. Paget's: refer or bisphosphonate per specialist. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Otitis externa
tools.evidence: Management per CKS Otitis externa.

options.label: Topical treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical acetic acid 2% or topical antibiotic (e.g. gentamicin/hydrocortisone or neomycin) for 7 days. Avoid water in ear.
2. Consider ear wick if canal swollen. Oral flucloxacillin if cellulitis. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Otitis media
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Mastoiditis (postauricular swelling, protrusion), facial palsy, intracranial complications, recurrent AOM (≥3 in 6 months or ≥4 in 12 months). Consider grommets. NICE NG91.

tools.title: Sinusitis

options.label: Likely viral (<10 days)
options.guidance:

options.label: Persistent or severe
options.guidance:

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Orbital/cranial complications, frontal swelling, severe headache, double vision, reduced consciousness.
2. Consider 2WW if chronic sinusitis or recurrent. NICE NG79, NG12.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCPCH):
1. Treatment: Single dose of Dexamethasone (0.15 mg/kg) - can use soluble tablets (e.g. 500mcg/tablet) mixed in water.
2. Note: All children with croup should receive a steroid dose as it reduces future severity.
3. Safety-net: Return if stridor at rest or increased work of breathing.

options.label: Moderate / Severe (Stridor at rest / Recession)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Immediate hospital referral (A&E). Avoid upsetting the child (no tongue depressors).

options.label: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss

options.label: Unilateral Pulsatile Tinnitus
options.guidance:

options.label: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction

options.label: TSH >10

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

2. 5 mins observation: No respiratory effort, no palpable pulse, fixed dilated pupils.
3. Documentation: Record time of death and clinical findings clearly.

tools.title: Bereavement – support
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

options.label: Expected death

options.label: Suture Removal Timings
options.guidance:

2. Scalp: 7-10 days.
3. Trunk / Arms: 10-14 days.
4. Legs / Extensor Surfaces: 14 days.
5. Note: Remove alternate sutures first if wound tension is high.

options.label: Wound Dressing Selection
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dry/Sutured: Film (Tegaderm) or simple island dressing.
2. Sloughy: Hydrogel (Intrasite).
3. Highly Exudative: Foam (Allevyn) or Alginate.
4. Infected: Honey (Medihoney) or Silver dressings.

tools.title: Acne  getting the management spot on – Management
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild (comedones)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Topical: adapalene 0.1% or benzoyl peroxide 5% OD. If inadequate after 12 weeks add topical antibiotic (e.g. clindamycin). NICE NG198.

options.label: Moderate (inflammatory)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Fixed combination: adapalene + benzoyl peroxide, or topical abx + benzoyl peroxide. If inadequate: oral doxycycline 100 mg OD 12 weeks (or lymecycline). NICE NG198.

options.label: Severe or scarring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer dermatology for oral isotretinoin. Exclude pregnancy; contraception. Do not offer oral antibiotic long-term as monotherapy. NICE NG198.

options.label: When to refer / pregnancy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Severe, scarring, or failed oral antibiotic. Isotretinoin: pregnancy prevention programme; two forms contraception.
2. Pregnancy: Topical only; avoid oral tetracyclines, isotretinoin. Azithromycin if needed. NICE NG198.

tools.title: Alcohol use disorders
tools.evidence: Management per NG115 and CKS Alcohol.

options.label: Holistic Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Stages of Change**: Identify where the patient is (Pre-contemplation to Maintenance).
2. **Harm Reduction**: Reducing units, switching to lower ABV, safe drinking intervals. 
3. **Biological**: Supervised detox if dependent (≥10 units/day or morning shakes) followed by anti-craving meds.
4. **Psychosocial**: Engagement with community services (AA, SMART Recovery) and addressing 'dual diagnosis' (co-morbid anxiety/depression).

options.label: Withdrawal Severity & Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Severity: 
   - Mild (CIWA <10): Supportive, vitamins only.
   - Mod/Severe (CIWA ≥10): Chlordiazepoxide regime.
2. **Wernicke's Triad**: Ophthalmoplegia, Ataxia, Confusion. 
3. **CRITICAL**: Give Pabrinex (Thiamine) BEFORE Glucose to prevent precipitating Wernicke's. NICE CG115.

options.label: Anti-Craving Pharmacotherapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Acamprosate**: 666mg tds. Start day 1 of abstinence.
2. **Naltrexone**: 50mg OD. Monitor LFTs.
3. **Disulfiram**: Specialist only. NICE CG115.

tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

tools.title: Management of insomnia – Management
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Sleep Specialist Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Principle**: Distinguish between Primary Insomnia and secondary to comorbidities (Pain/OSA/Depression).
2. **Therapy**: **CBT-I is the gold standard 1st-line treatment**—superior long-term results to pharmacological options.
3. **Biological**: Circadian rhythm stabilization (melatonin) and conservative use of sedative hypnotics for short-term relief only.
4. **Environment**: Optimization of the sleep environment and addressing 'sleep effort' (the paradoxical anxiety about falling asleep).

options.label: Behavioural Interventions
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Sleep Restriction**: Limit time in bed to actual sleep duration (min 5h). Increases 'sleep drive'.
2. **Stimulus Control**: Leave bed if awake for >20 mins. Re-associate bed with sleep only.
3. **Cognitive**: Challenging 'catastrophic' thoughts about sleep loss impact.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

tools.evidence: Podcasts will cover clinical tips and hacks as well as hot topics to help make our lives a wee bit easier, but ultimately to help improve the lives of our patients in primary care. In this podcast, I'm [Name], the Priffff.

options.label: Assessment

options.label: Management

options.label: Anaemia / clotting
options.guidance:

options.label: Malignancy / cytopenia

tools.title: Travel – DVT
tools.evidence: NICE NG158: Wells score for DVT/PE; D-dimer (age-adjusted if >50). Imaging within 4h if likely DVT; CTPA for PE. DOAC 3 months minimum; extend if unprovoked or high risk.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):
1. Action: Urgent Proximal Leg US within 4h (or interim anticoagulation if wait >4h).
2. Result: If US negative but D-dimer positive, repeat US in 6-8 days.

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Immediate: CTPA (Computed Tomographic Pulmonary Angiography). Interim anticoagulation (e.g. Apixaban 10mg bd) if scan delayed >1h.
2. V/Q Scan: Preferred if renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe allergy to contrast.
3. Note: If PE likely, assess PESI score for suitability of outpatient management.

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).
2. Refer: Anticoagulation failure, thrombophilia testing (young, family history), cancer-associated. NICE NG158.

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 months (provoked/low risk), 6 months+ or indefinite (unprovoked or recurrence). NICE NG158.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

tools.title: Vitamin B12 – replacement
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: B12 Deficiency - Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-dietary (e.g. Pernicious Anaemia): Hydroxocobalamin 1mg IM every other day for 2 weeks (loading), then 1mg IM every 3 months for life.
2. Dietary: Oral cyanocobalamin 50-150mcg daily between meals, or two 1mg injections per year.
3. Monitoring: Reticulocyte count at 7-10 days; Hb/MCV at 8 weeks.
4. Review: Exclude co-existing Iron/Folate deficiency if response sub-optimal. NICE CKS.

options.label: Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Confirm deficiency; treat cause. Magnesium: replace orally (e.g. magnesium glycerophosphate). Vitamin C: dietary + supplement if deficient. Vitamin K: phytonadione if bleeding/anticoagulant reversal. Zinc: oral replacement. Multiple: address diet; replace as per levels. NICE CKS, BNF.

tools.title: Vitamin D
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Deficiency (<30 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Loading: 300,000 IU total over 6-10 weeks (e.g. 20,000 IU twice weekly for 7 weeks or 50,000 IU weekly for 6 weeks).
2. Maintenance: 800-2000 IU daily (or 20,000-40,000 IU monthly) lifelong if risk factors persist.
3. Safety: Avoid loading if primary hyperparathyroidism or renal stones suspected. ROS Guidelines.

options.label: Insufficiency (30-50 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Strategy: Advise dietary sources (oily fish, eggs) and safe sun exposure.
2. Supplement: 800-1000 IU daily as maintenance; loading not routinely required unless symptomatic or high-risk of progression. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Blepharitis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Mild/Moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Lid hygiene (warm compresses). Preservative-free lubricants (e.g. Hylo-Forte, Viscotears). Ointment at night (e.g. Lacri-Lube). NICE CKS Dry Eye.

options.label: Severe or refractory
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to Ophthalmology. Consider punctal plugs or ciclosporin drops. Exclude Sjogren's syndrome (check ANA, Ro/La).

tools.title: Conjunctivitis
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Bacterial Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Chloramphenicol 0.5% drops 2-hourly for 2 days then qds. Fusidic acid if pregnant. Safety-net for pain/vision loss. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected Corneal Ulcer/Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Contact lens wearer? Painful? Fluorescein staining positive? Emergency Ophthalmology referral (same day). Avoid steroids.

options.label: Scleritis (Deep pain)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Deep, boring eye pain. Systemic associations (rheumatoid). Urgent Ophthalmology referral (within 24-48h). NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / red eye warning
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: Pain, photophobia, reduced vision, contact lens wear, trauma, chemical injury.
2. Urgent: Viral keratitis (dendritic), scleritis, acute glaucoma. Avoid steroids until cause known. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Corneal Ulcers
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Suspected Microbial Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IMMEDIATE: Emergency Same-Day Ophthalmology referral (A&E eye clinic).
2. First Aid: Stop contact lens wear immediately; do not patch the eye.
3. Note: High risk of permanent vision loss/perforation within 24-48h if untreated. Moorfields Guidelines.

options.label: Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Viral/Allergic: cool compresses, lubricants. Bacterial: Topical antibiotic (Chloramphenicol 0.5%) if severe/persistent. Safety-net for 'red eye' warning signs. NICE CKS.

options.label: Glaucoma (Chronic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Prostaglandin analogues (e.g. Latanoprost) first-line. Monitor IOP and visual fields annually. Urgent referral if Acute Angle Closure suspected. NICE NG81.

tools.title: Open-Angle Glaucoma
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Newly diagnosed/Suspected
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to secondary care for diagnosis and treatment initiation. First-line usually Prostaglandin analogue (e.g. Latanoprost). NICE NG81.

options.label: Community Monitoring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check IOP, visual fields, and adherence. Beta-blockers (e.g. Timolol) used as adjunctive; check for contraindications (Asthma/Heart Block).

tools.title: Ophthalmological Emergencies
tools.evidence: Management per NICE CKS and Local formulary.

options.label: Sudden painless loss of vision (RAO)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Suspected Retinal Artery Occlusion. Emergency (999 or Eye Casualty). Stroke symptoms? TIA workup needed.

options.label: Painful red eye + nausea (Acute Glaucoma)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Emergency referral. Fixed semi-dilated pupil. Give Acetazolamide 500mg IV/PO if remote from hospital (per local policy).

options.label: Floaters and flashes (Detachment)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Retinal detachment until proven otherwise. Urgent (same day) Ophthalmology review.
